TheoremLet \(B=D/\langle\tau\rangle\), a genus-3 curve over \(\mathbb Q\) with good reduction outside \(\{2,3\}\). The correspondence \(\mathcal T=\tfrac12q_*(\sigma_*+\sigma_*^{-1})q^*\) is an endomorphism of \(\operatorname{Jac}B\) defined over \(K\), satisfying \(\mathcal T^3-3\mathcal T+1=0\). Moreover \(\operatorname{End}^0_K(\operatorname{Jac}B)=K\) and \(\operatorname{End}^0_{\mathbb Q}(\operatorname{Jac}B)=\mathbb Q\).

The proof has three parts. First, \(\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb Q(\zeta_9)/\mathbb Q)\) sends \(\sigma\) to \(\sigma^a\), so \(\sigma+\sigma^{-1}\) is fixed exactly by \(\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb Q(\zeta_9)/K)\), and \(\mathcal T\) is defined over \(K\). Second, all of \(H^1(D)\) lies in the primitive characters, because the quotient by \(\mu_9\) and the intermediate cubic cover both have genus 0. On the \(a\)-part of \(H^1(B)\), \(\mathcal T\) acts by \(\zeta^a+\zeta^{-a}\). Its eigenvalues are therefore the three conjugates of \(\theta\), and the cubic relation holds on \(H^1\), hence in \(\operatorname{End}\). Third, the upper bounds follow as in §69 from Frobenius fields. The zeta function of \(B\) equals that of \(C\) at the nine primes above, so the subfield certificate of §69 applies verbatim to \(B\).

For \(C\) itself, the same conclusion follows once \(\operatorname{Jac}C\sim_{\mathbb Q}\operatorname{Jac}B\) is established, which is Laga–Shnidman's identification and is supported here by 27 of 27 exact counts. This is the algebra-to-geometry step Part XVI asked for, carried out on cohomology. The recovered field is realized by an explicit correspondence. Its smallest field of definition is \(K\). Its action on \(H^1\) produces the Frobenius element \(t_p\in\mathcal O_K\), whose norm is the spectrum.

71. Status after Part XVI

Part XVI's computations reproduce exactly, from a counter that shares no code with it. Its field-of-definition reading is now a theorem with a falsifiable consequence: \(a_1=a_2=0\) at every inert prime. That consequence holds in all 38 inert cases, as the norm law holds in all 12 split cases. Its "hidden endomorphism" is placed precisely. \(\operatorname{End}^0_{\mathbb Q}=\mathbb Q\) is proved, and \(\operatorname{End}^0_K=K\) is proved for the cover quotient \(B\). The proof uses the explicit correspondence, whose cohomological action produces the Frobenius elements \(t_p\) without any search.

The remaining gap is the isogeny \(\operatorname{Jac}C\sim_{\mathbb Q}\operatorname{Jac}B\), equivalently Laga–Shnidman's birational map. It can be closed by a Faltings–Serre computation. The cover has good reduction outside \(\{2,3\}\), and the quartic model of \(C\) is smooth at every prime from 5 to 397 (hf_check/bad_primes.py), so both conductors are expected to be supported on \(\{2,3\}\), and a finite list of traces at primes up to an explicit bound would decide it, and the counter here computes those traces in seconds. Part XVI's own suggestion, a curve with no automorphisms whose Jacobian splits over \(\mathbb Q\), also remains open, and the certificate of §65 applies to it unchanged.

72. Part XVII. The quotient isomorphism, proved independently

The parallel session's Part XVII closes the gap of §71 by an explicit map instead of Faltings–Serre. On \(D_t:\;Y^9=\frac{x+1}{x-1}\big(\frac{x+t}{x-t}\big)^3\) it sets \(a=Y^3\frac{x-t}{x+t}\), \(z=a+a^{-1}\), \(W=\frac{1-ua^3}{a^2}Y+a^2(1-ua^{-3})Y^{-1}\) with \(u=\frac{t-1}{t+1}\), and \(y_C=\frac{W-uz-1}{z+u}\), \(x_C=y_C+z\). It claims that \((x_C,y_C)\) satisfies the quartic \(C_u\). Its suite passes in an isolated copy: the symbolic quotient, smoothness, 15 paired counts, 5 Weil factorizations, 106 Frobenius-power checks and a trivial \(PGL_3(\mathbb F_5)\) stabilizer. All 1,348 earlier files are preserved.

MeasuredI proved the identity in a different representation (gc_check/quotient_map.py). Since \(a^3=\frac{x+1}{x-1}\), we have \(x=\frac{a^3+1}{a^3-1}\), and the function field of \(D_t\) is the cubic extension \(\mathbb Q(t,a)[Y]/(Y^3-c)\) with \(c=a\frac{x+t}{x-t}\). Every element is a triple over the rational field \(\mathbb Q(t,a)\), with \(Y^{-1}=Y^2/c\). In this algebra, for generic \(t\), three things hold. \(W\) is invariant under \(\tau:(a,Y)\mapsto(a^{-1},Y^{-1})\). \(W^3-3D(z)W-D(z)(z^2-uz-2)=0\) with \(D(z)=1+u^2-u(z^3-3z)\). And \(y_C^4-x_Cy_C^3-ux_C^3-3y_C^2+2ux_C+uy_C+1=0\) in all three components. Degrees finish the proof. \([\mathbb Q(a):\mathbb Q(z)]=2\) and \([\mathbb Q(D):\mathbb Q(a)]=3\), so the \(\tau\)-invariant field has degree 3 over \(\mathbb Q(z)\). At \(u=2\), specializing the monic cubic to \(z=0\) gives \(W^3-15W+10\), which is Eisenstein at 5, so the cubic is irreducible over \(\mathbb Q(z)\) by Gauss. Hence \(\mathbb Q(z,W)\) is the whole invariant field. It equals \(\mathbb Q(x_C,y_C)\), since \(z=x_C-y_C\) and \(W=y_C(z+u)+uz+1\). That gives \(D_t/\langle\tau\rangle\cong_{\mathbb Q}C_u\), for \(t=-3\) in particular.

TheoremFor the automorphism-free quartic \(C=C_2\): \(\operatorname{End}^0_K(\operatorname{Jac}C)=K=\mathbb Q(\zeta_9)^+\) and \(\operatorname{End}^0_{\mathbb Q}(\operatorname{Jac}C)=\mathbb Q\). The real multiplication is realized by the correspondence \(\mathcal T=\tfrac12q_*(\sigma_*+\sigma_*^{-1})q^*\) carried through the isomorphism. This is the theorem of §70 for \(B=D/\tau\), now transferred to \(C\) without conditions. The 27 matching counts of §70 become a consistency check, no longer evidence.

73. A symmetry-free curve with a split Jacobian, checked

Part XVII also gives the example §§66 and 71 asked for: a smooth plane quartic \(C^\star\) with no automorphisms whose Jacobian splits over \(\mathbb Q\). It is \[X^4-6X^3Y+2X^3-27X^2Y^2-18X^2Y-3X^2+54XY^3-31X+162Y^4+108Y^3+837Y^2+186Y+31=0.\] It comes with a map to \(E:V^2=U^3-29U-59\), given by \(t=\frac{X-1-6Y}{3Y^2}\), \(U=t-3\), \(W=1+Yt\), \(V=-(W^3+UW+1)\).

Measured(gc_check/split_quartic.py, split_zeta.py, abs_simple.py.)
Smoothness: the projective closure is smooth over \(\mathbb Q\), since Gröbner bases on all three affine charts equal \(\{1\}\). Below 200, the model is singular only at \(2,3,29,31,43,83\).
The map: \(V^2-(U^3-29U-59)\) vanishes modulo the quartic. \(U\) has degree 6 on \(C^\star\): the pencil of conics \(X=1+6Y+3(c+3)Y^2\) meets the quartic in 8 points, 2 of them fixed at the base point \((1,0)\). So the map has degree exactly 3.
The curve \(E\): conductor \(14276=2^2\cdot43\cdot83\) and \(j=168576768/3569\). The \(j\)-invariant is not integral, so \(E\) has no CM.
Zeta functions: an independent GP counter gives the numerators at all 12 good primes \(5\le p\le59\). \(1-a_p(E)T+pT^2\) divides each one, and \(P_{A,5}\), \(P_{A,11}\) agree with Part XVII.
Absolute simplicity: \(A_p\) is ordinary with irreducible \(\chi_p\) at 9 primes. At each of them no ratio of Frobenius roots is a root of unity, since \(\operatorname{Res}_y(\chi(y),\chi(xy))/(x-1)^4\) has no cyclotomic factor. So \(A_p\) is absolutely simple at all 9.
Endomorphisms: their Frobenius fields have the quadratic subfields \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt{13})\) at 5, 7 and 13, \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt{10})\) at 11, and \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt7)\), \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt{30})\), \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt{381})\), \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt{373})\) and \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt{97})\) at the rest. \(\operatorname{End}^0_{\overline{\mathbb Q}}(A)\) embeds into each of these fields, so \(\operatorname{End}^0_{\overline{\mathbb Q}}(A)=\mathbb Q\), with seven witnesses beyond Part XVII's two.

I checked the automorphism argument and it holds. \(\operatorname{End}^0_{\overline{\mathbb Q}}(\operatorname{Jac}C^\star)=\mathbb Q\times\mathbb Q\) has unit group \(\{\pm1\}^2\) in any order, and by Torelli \(\operatorname{Aut}(C^\star)\times\{\pm1\}=\operatorname{Aut}(J,\theta)\). So a nontrivial automorphism would be an involution acting by \(-1\) on one factor. Its quotient would be a degree-2 map to an elliptic curve. That map is optimal (2 is prime), so by Kani it embeds an elliptic subvariety with induced polarization of degree 2. The degree-3 map is also optimal, since its degree is prime and a curve of genus 3 cannot map with degree 1 to an elliptic curve. It gives an elliptic subvariety of induced degree 3. With \(\operatorname{End}^0=\mathbb Q\times\mathbb Q\) the elliptic subvariety is unique, a contradiction. So \(\operatorname{Aut}_{\overline{\mathbb Q}}(C^\star)=1\) and \(\operatorname{Jac}C^\star\sim_{\mathbb Q}E\times A\), with \(A\) geometrically simple and \(\operatorname{End}^0_{\overline{\mathbb Q}}(A)=\mathbb Q\).

74. Finding the elliptic factor blind

Part XVII names the next capability: recover the elliptic quotient from the quartic alone, without being told \(E\). The target, at least, can be recovered from the zeta functions.

Measured(gc_check/blind_E.py; \(E\) is never an input.) At every good prime where \(P_{C^\star,p}\) has exactly one quadratic factor over \(\mathbb Z\), that factor must be the elliptic one: a degree-2 Weil polynomial is irreducible, and its cofactor is then an irreducible quartic. This fixes \(a_p\) blind at 9 primes: \(a_5=-3\), \(a_7=-2\), \(a_{11}=-1\), \(a_{13}=0\), \(a_{23}=-1\), \(a_{37}=8\), \(a_{41}=1\), \(a_{47}=4\), \(a_{59}=0\). Bad reduction of the Jacobian requires a singular plane model, so its bad primes lie in \(\{2,3,29,31,43,83\}\). A bounded search of \(y^2=x^3+Ax+B\) with \(|A|\le300\) and \(|B|\le600\) took 145 seconds over about 866,000 curves. It kept only curves with conductor supported on those primes and matching all nine traces, and exactly one survived: \(A=-29\), \(B=-59\), conductor 14276. Its factor then divides \(P_{C^\star,p}\) at all 12 good primes, including the three (17, 19 and 53) where the factorization had left \(a_p\) ambiguous.

This is recovery of the target, not of the map, and it has two limits. The search needs a height bound, and it succeeded because \(E\) is small. And agreement at finitely many primes identifies an isogeny class only up to a Faltings–Serre bound. Here the explicit map of §73 settles it. The remaining step is constructing the degree-3 morphism once \(E\) is known. A natural route is to search for functions of degree 6 on \(C^\star\) in pencils of conics through a point, since the Part XVII map is of exactly this form. Its fibres must be the pullbacks of the 2-torsion-invariant pairs on \(E\).

75. Status after Part XVII

The open gap of Part XVI is closed by an explicit isomorphism, \(D_{-3}/\tau\cong_{\mathbb Q}C_2\), proved here independently for generic \(t\). The automorphism-free quartic therefore has real multiplication by \(\mathcal O_K\) defined exactly over \(K\), and only scalar endomorphisms over \(\mathbb Q\). That is a complete, unconditional instance of a hidden operator field inside a \(\mathbb Q\)-simple object.

The complementary example now exists and is verified: an automorphism-free quartic whose Jacobian splits over \(\mathbb Q\), through a degree-3 correspondence. Its elliptic factor can be recovered from zeta data alone by the procedure of §74. Together the two examples bound the program's question from both sides. Splittings and endomorphism fields are both visible in Frobenius data. Proving that they exist still requires an explicit correspondence, and in both examples that correspondence has now been written down.

76. Part XVIII. The map-discovery engine, checked

The parallel session's Part XVIII recovers the degree-3 map \(C^\star\to E\) from the quartic equation alone. It finds a rational point \(P=(1,0)\) and its tangent \(X=1+6Y+O(Y^2)\), substitutes \(X=1+6Y+TY^2\), divides out the base factor, and completes the square of the resulting sextic in \(Y\) over \(\mathbb Q(T)\). The \(Y\)-dependent remainder vanishes, and the rest normalizes to \(E\). Its suite passes 12 of 12 tests in an isolated copy, and all 1,375 earlier files are preserved.

MeasuredEvery identity holds exactly (mf_check/identities.py). These are the square completion (1), the map \(U=\frac{X-1-6Y-9Y^2}{3Y^2}\), \(V=-\frac{X^3-9X^2Y-9XY-3X+81Y^3+54Y^2+18Y+2}{27Y^3}\) modulo the quartic, and the pulled-back differential \(f^*(dU/2V)=-27\,X\,dX/F_Y\). The rediscovered \(V\) is identical on \(C^\star\) to the \(V\) of §73, so the search finds the same map. The projector \(e_f=\tfrac13f^*f_*\) is correct as stated: \(f_*f^*=[3]\) on \(E\) gives \((f^*f_*)^2=3f^*f_*\). Its denominator 3 is the degree of the correspondence.

MeasuredPart XVIII's Cartier table covers three primes. I recomputed the Hasse–Witt matrix in the Stöhr–Voloch form at all 12 good primes \(5\le p\le59\) (mf_check/hasse_witt.py). Here \(C(\omega_{kl})=\sum M_{(i,j),(k,l)}\omega_{ij}\), with \(M_{(i,j),(k,l)}\) the coefficient of \(x^{pi-k}y^{pj-l}\) in \(F^{p-1}\) and \(\omega_{ij}=x^{i-1}y^{j-1}dx/F_y\). At every one of these primes, \(\omega_{21}=X\,dX/F_Y\) is an eigenvector with eigenvalue \(a_p(E)\bmod p\). At \(p=13\) and \(59\), where \(E\) is supersingular, it is killed. This is the expected compatibility, since the Cartier operator commutes with \(f^*\) and acts on \(E\)'s differential by the Hasse invariant. The arithmetic side therefore identifies the elliptic differential line at every good prime, before any map is known.

77. The structure behind the pencil

The pencil Part XVIII uses has an intrinsic description that its affine normal form hides. Projectively it is \(\{MN-u\ell^2\}\). Here \(M:X-6Y-Z=0\) is the tangent at \(P=(1{:}0{:}1)\), \(\ell:Y=0\) is a second line through \(P\), and \(N:Z=0\) is the line at infinity.

MeasuredTwo facts make this canonical. First, the line \(\ell\) meets \(C^\star\) in \(P\) and the triple \(X^3+3X^2-31=0\), which is irreducible over \(\mathbb Q\). That triple is \(D_3=f^{-1}(O_E)\), the fibre over the origin, so \(u=MN/\ell^2\in L(2D_3)\) and \(u=x\circ f\) up to an affine change. Second, the three members of the pencil over the 2-torsion abscissae \(e^3-29e-59=0\) are totally tangent conics: over \(\mathbb Q(e)\), the residual sextic of \(X=1+6Y+(9+3e)Y^2\) is an exact square. Their contact divisors are the fibres over the 2-torsion points.

The general recipe follows. Take a rational point \(P\) with tangent \(M\), and a line \(\ell\) through \(P\) whose residual triple \(D_3\) is to be a fibre. The conics tangent to \(C\) at \(P\) divided by \(\ell^2\) span \(L(2D_3)\), which has dimension 4. Inside it, the elliptic pencils are \(\{MN-u\ell^2\}\) for the right line \(N\). Equivalently, they are the pencils that contain \(\ell^2\) and three totally tangent conics.

78. A projectively invariant discovery engine

Negative resultThe Part XVIII engine fixes \(N\) as the line at infinity and needs an integral point. So it depends on the choice of coordinates, not just on the curve. Run unmodified on \(C^\star\) (mf_check/stress.py), it succeeds after both affine changes of coordinates tested. It fails after all three non-affine changes in \(PGL_3(\mathbb Z)\), \(Z\mapsto Z+Y\), \(Z\mapsto Z+X-Y\) and \((X,Z)\mapsto(X+Y,Z-Y)\), although the curve and the map are unchanged.

mf_check/invariant_engine.py searches the intrinsic data instead. It ranges over projective rational points \(P\), lines \(\ell\) through \(P\), and free lines \(N\) with \(N(P)\ne0\), all of small height. It never uses an affine normal form, and the target is used only to grade the output. A candidate pencil is kept when two tests pass.

(a) At two specializations \(u_0\), the fibre sextic has a quadratic subfield, since \(K(C)\supset K(E)\supset K(u)\) makes the fibre field contain \(\mathbb Q(V(u_0))\).

(b) The fibre discriminant in \(u\) contains factors of total degree 3 with multiplicity at least 3. These are the totally tangent members of §77.

From (b) the cubic \(c(u)\) is read off. The quadratic subfield at \(u_0\) fixes the twist \(\kappa\equiv d_0\,c(u_0)\) modulo squares. Then \(E:\kappa V^2=c(u)\) is produced by ellfromeqn and reduced to its minimal model.

MeasuredOn \(C^\star\) and on all three projective transforms where Part XVIII failed, the engine returns \([0,0,0,-29,-59]\), conductor 14276, with \(j\) and \(a_p\) matching. It needs between 1 and 21 pencils and at most 0.3 seconds (mf_check/invariant_engine.json). On the Part XVIII family I applied a random non-affine element of \(PGL_3(\mathbb Z)\) with entries in \(\{-1,0,1\}\) to each of the 8 smooth members (mf_check/benchmark.py). Part XVIII's engine then finds 1 of 8. The invariant engine finds 8 of 8, each in the correct isogeny class, in at most 0.4 seconds.

The first run missed one case, \(E:y^2=x^3-35x-62\). This curve has a rational 2-torsion point, so \(c(u)\) splits as a linear factor times a quadratic, and the recovery step was then looking only for an irreducible cubic. Taking \(c(u)\) as the product of all high-multiplicity factors, of total degree 3, fixed it.

The negative controls search exhaustively, with no early stop, at the same heights. One is the Laga–Shnidman quartic \(C_2\), whose Jacobian is \(\mathbb Q\)-simple by §67 (4 rational points, 123 pencils). The other is a random smooth quartic (2 points, 63 pencils). Both give no hits.

The engine still needs a rational point and lines of small height. Its scope is quartics with a rational point whose elliptic quotient is realized by a degree-3 map, and it is a search, not a decision procedure. Within that scope it no longer depends on coordinates, and it fails safe on curves without an elliptic factor.

79. Status after Part XVIII

Part XVIII's identities, map, differential and projector are all confirmed, and its Cartier recovery holds at every good prime tested. Its engine works in the coordinates it was built for and breaks under projective changes of coordinates. The cause is that the pencil's third line had been fixed as the line at infinity. With that line searched, the engine depends only on the curve. It recovers the correct elliptic factor in every transformed case and returns nothing on the controls.

The structure behind it is now explicit: the fibre over \(O_E\) is the residual triple of a line through a rational point, and the 2-torsion fibres are contact divisors of totally tangent conics. That points to removing the last height dependence. Totally tangent conics through a fixed tangency are cut out by algebraic conditions, which can be solved rather than searched. Solving them would turn this engine into an algorithm that finds the pencil, not merely tests it.

80. Part XIX. The contact-conic incidence scheme

TheoremLet \(C:F(L,H,Z)=0\) be a smooth plane quartic with a rational smooth point \(P=(0:0:1)\) and tangent \(H=0\). Every nonsingular conic through \(P\) with this tangent, normalized at \(P\), is \(Q_{a,b,c}=HZ+aL^2+bLH+cH^2\) with \(a\ne0\). Parametrize it by \([L:H:Z]=[-t:-t^2:a+bt+ct^2]\). The residual intersection polynomial is \(G_{a,b,c}(t)=t^{-2}F(-t,-t^2,a+bt+ct^2)\), of degree at most six. Where its sixth-degree coefficient is nonzero, \(Q_{a,b,c}\cdot C\) is twice an effective divisor if and only if \(G/g_6\) is a monic cubic square. Writing \(h_i=g_i/g_6\), the cubic is uniquely determined by \(s_2=h_5/2\), \(s_1=(h_4-s_2^2)/2\), \(s_0=(h_3-2s_2s_1)/2\), and the contact equations are exactly \(h_2-s_1^2-2s_2s_0=h_1-2s_1s_0=h_0-s_0^2=0\). Clearing denominators gives three algebraic equations in the three conic coefficients, not a bounded-height line search.

81. Incidence lifting reconstructs the hidden rational pencil

Current-edition correction. Corrected by §§84 and 96: eight modular candidates were printed, but only six satisfy the nondegenerate-conic condition. Two had a=0 and singular Jacobians.

The correct degree-three elliptic map induces a conic pencil \(HZ+b_0LH+c_0H^2+z(L+sH)^2\). Its direction in contact-coefficient space obeys \(d_b^2=4d_ad_c\). The solver first finds solutions to the three contact equations over a small finite field, detects triples on a line with that rank-one direction, Hensel-lifts their coefficient triples, and rationally reconstructs the direction and anchor from their differences. Every candidate is subsequently checked over \(\mathbb Q\). This replaces enumeration of rational pencils by algebraic incidence and \(p\)-adic lifting. The chosen prime and precision bound the run, but not the height of the reconstructed rational pencil; a finite unsuccessful search does not certify nonexistence.

MeasuredOn the split genus-three quartic \(C^\star\) of §73, the contact equations have eight nonsingular solutions modulo 17, including exactly one rank-one-direction line containing three: \((a,b,c)=(1,0,0),(7,0,0),(16,0,0)\). Lifting to \(17^8=6,975,757,441\) reconstructs \(b=c=0\) over \(\mathbb Q\). The contact roots satisfy \(z^3+27z^2-18z-27=0\), recovered directly from the original quartic rather than from a supplied elliptic curve.

82. The exact degree-three map from contact square completion

Constructive theoremNormalize the recovered line so its conics are \(HZ+zL^2=0\), and set \(z=-HZ/L^2\), \(t=H/L\) on the source curve. If the residual sextic has the exact identity \(G(z,t)/g_6=S_3(z,t)^2+R(z)\), with \(R\) a separable cubic, then \(w=S_3(z,t)\) gives \(w^2=-R(z)\). Writing \(-R(z)=c_3z^3+c_2z^2+c_1z+c_0\), the functions \(U=c_3z+c_2/3\), \(V=c_3w\) satisfy the short Weierstrass equation with \(A=c_3c_1-c_2^2/3\), \(B=c_3^2c_0-c_2c_3c_1/3+2c_2^3/27\). An irreducible specialization of the degree-six polynomial \(G(z,t)\) proves \([\mathbb Q(C):\mathbb Q(z)]=6\), while the cubic defines a quadratic field over \(\mathbb Q(z)\); the induced map has degree three. All equalities are checked by exact polynomial arithmetic.

Exact resultHere \(G=(t^3+9t^2-3zt-9z-27)^2+27(z^3+27z^2-18z-27)\). Its specialization at \(z=1\) is \(t^6+18t^5+75t^4-126t^3-639t^2+216t+837\), irreducible over \(\mathbb Q\). The resulting target, after a rational short-model scaling, is \(V^2=U^3-29U-59\), and the rational map is identical to §76. It gives the global correspondence \(Z_f=f^*f_*\) with \(Z_f^2=3Z_f\), so \(Z_f/3\) is a rational Jacobian projector even though the curve has no automorphism inducing the map.

83. Reproducibility and the remaining geometric frontier

Current-edition correction. Corrected by §§84 and 96: the benchmark had 29 successful runs but only eight distinct curve classes, including repeated copies of C⋆.

MeasuredThe algebraic contact-incidence solver recovered an exact degree-three map on all 12 random integral projective transformations of \(C^\star\), all nine smooth unrelated cubic-cover family members, and eight additional non-affine projective transformations of these family members. It independently derived the correct target in each case, not just its zeta traces. A dedicated independent checker rederived the pencil, the function-field square completion and the degree witness from a JSON certificate without importing the discovery code. Four negative-control point tests over primes 17, 31 and 43 produced no false hit; those finite tests are not nonexistence proofs. The standalone source, exact receipts, and test suite are under contact_foundry_xix/.

ScopeThis removes the need for a height bound on the rational pencil coefficients, but retains the requirement of a supplied rational point, a suitable nonsingular modular reduction with three split contact points, and a recoverable rank-one direction in the chosen frame. The search is not complete for arbitrary quartics. The next mathematically substantial extension is to work over residue-field extensions and closed points, and to replace the distinguished base point by a degree-three divisor found through Riemann–Roch. The larger Foundry objective is to turn such incidence-elimination procedures into a general discovery engine for algebraic correspondences, not merely a fast map checker.

84. Part XX. The contact solver of Part XIX, checked

The parallel session's Part XIX replaces the line-height search of §78 with a contact-incidence solver. That solver enumerates the contact scheme modulo a small prime, Hensel-lifts three collinear contact points and rationally reconstructs the elliptic pencil through them. Its suite passes 8 of 8 tests in an isolated copy. Its three benchmarks reproduce here at 12 of 12, 9 of 9 and 8 of 8, and its exact checker accepts both stored receipts and a freshly generated one. The measured cost per orbit transform is 0.44–1.28 s on this machine, against the reported 0.34–0.98 s.

MeasuredI re-derived the reference computation with code that imports nothing from the package (exact_foundry_xx/indep_xix.py). In the frame \(L=Y\), \(H=X-6Y-Z\), \(Z=Z\) at \(P_1=(1{:}0{:}1)\), the cleared contact numerators \(\mathcal R_2,\mathcal R_1,\mathcal R_0\) of (80.5) have total degrees 12, 15 and 18. Modulo 17, on the open set \(a\,g_6\ne0\), they have exactly six common zeros, all with invertible Jacobian. Exactly one rank-one line passes through three of them, \(\{(1,0,0),(7,0,0),(16,0,0)\}\). Restricted to \(b=c=0\), the gcd of the three numerators is \(6912\,(a^3+27a^2-18a-27)\). The identity (82.6) holds exactly, \(G(1,t)\) is irreducible, and the substitution \(z=-3U-9\) sends the contact cubic to \(-27(U^3-29U-59)\). So the three contact conics are the fibres over the nonzero 2-torsion points, as claimed. The map (82.7) satisfies the Weierstrass equation modulo the quartic.

Correction§81 says the contact scheme has "eight nonsingular solutions" at 17. The enumeration in find_contact_points does not impose \(a\ne0\). It returns eight points, two of which, \((0,10,2)\) and \((0,14,9)\), have \(a=0\). These are the reducible conics \(H(Z+bL+cH)\) that (80.1) excludes, and both have singular Jacobian (determinant \(\equiv0\bmod17\)). The correct statement is six solutions in the chart, all nonsingular.

Correction§83 calls the nine family members "smooth unrelated" curves with "nine distinct" targets. The member \((w,c)=(1,1)\) is \(C^\star\) itself, coefficient for coefficient. The member \((-1,1)\) is the image of \((1,-1)\) under \(Y\mapsto-Y\), which is why the target \(V^2=U^3-33U-63\) appears twice. The nine members are therefore eight projective classes, one of which is \(C^\star\). Of the 29 positive recoveries, 14 are copies of \(C^\star\) (12 orbit transforms, one family run and one scrambled run), and the benchmark contains eight distinct curves. No identity is affected. There is also a structural point. The family generator builds each quartic from the pencil at \((1{:}0{:}1)\), and every benchmark case is run at that point or its image. The experiments therefore test recovery at a point where a pencil is known to exist. They never test where else a pencil might exist, or prove that none exists anywhere.

85. Every degree-three elliptic subcover has exactly two collinear fibres

The base point of §80 is not an arbitrary rational point. Its role is fixed by the geometry of the map, and this section determines it.

Theorem 85.1Let \(C\subset\mathbb P^2_k\) be a smooth plane quartic over a field of characteristic zero, and let \(f:C\to E\) be a morphism of degree 3 to an elliptic curve. Then exactly two fibres of \(f\), counted with multiplicity, are contained in a line. The divisor \(Q_1+Q_2\) of their images is defined over \(k\). So either \(Q_1,Q_2\in E(k)\), or they are conjugate over a quadratic extension of \(k\).

The proof is as follows. Put \(V=H^0(\mathbb P^2,\mathcal O(1))\) and consider the evaluation map \(\mathrm{ev}:V\otimes\mathcal O_E\to f_*\mathcal O_C(1)\) of rank-3 bundles. Its determinant is a section of \(\det f_*\mathcal O_C(1)\). That bundle has degree \(\deg\mathcal O_C(1)+\deg\det f_*\mathcal O_C=4-\tfrac12\deg B_f=4-2=2\), because the branch divisor has degree \(2g_C-2-3(2g_E-2)=4\). At \(Q\), \(\mathrm{ev}\) fails to be an isomorphism exactly when a linear form vanishes on the scheme-theoretic fibre \(f^*Q\), that is, when the fibre lies on a line. The section is not identically zero. Suppose every fibre lay on a line \(\ell_Q\). The residual points \(\ell_Q\cdot C-f^*Q\) would then define a morphism \(E\to C\), which is constant by Riemann–Hurwitz. So every \(\ell_Q\) would pass through one point \(P_0\in C\). The fibres of \(f\) would then be the fibres of projection from \(P_0\), and \(E\) would be rational. Hence the zero divisor has degree exactly 2.

Derived(Corollary 85.2, base points.) For a collinear fibre \(f^*Q\subset\ell_Q\), put \(P_Q=\ell_Q\cdot C-f^*Q\). Then \(K_C\sim P_Q+f^*Q\), and \(P_Q\) is defined over \(k(Q)\). These two points are the only possible base points of the construction of §§80–82, for any choice of origin on \(E\). Pushing \(K_C\) forward gives \(f_*K_C\sim f(P_Q)+3Q\), so \[ f(P_Q)\oplus[3]Q=c_f\qquad\text{for both collinear fibres,} \] with \(c_f\in E(k)\) depending only on \(f\).

Measured(collinear_exact.py.) On \(C^\star\) the two collinear fibres are found and verified exactly. The fibre over \(Q_1=O\) is the residual cubic \(X^3+3X^2Z-31Z^3\) of the line \(Y=0\), with \(P_{Q_1}=P_1=(1{:}0{:}1)\). The fibre over \(Q_2=(-3,-1)\) lies on the line \(Z=0\), which cuts \(C^\star\) in \((3{:}1{:}0)\), \((-3{:}1{:}0)\) and the conjugate pair \(X^2-6XY-18Y^2=0\). On \((3{:}1{:}0)\) and on the conjugate pair, \(U\equiv-3\) and \(V\equiv-1\) exactly, so \(P_{Q_2}=P_2=(-3{:}1{:}0)\). The pushforward law holds as an exact check. A branch expansion at \(P_1\) gives \(f(P_1)=(7,-9)\). Also \(f(P_2)=(-3,1)=-Q_2\), and \(-Q_2\oplus[3]Q_2=[2]Q_2=(7,-9)\), so \(c_f=(7,-9)\) for both fibres. Up to height 12, \(C^\star\) has exactly three rational points: \(P_1\), \(P_2\) and \(R=(3{:}1{:}0)\), which lies inside the fibre over \(Q_2\). The second base point \(P_2\) appears nowhere in Part XIX.

RemarkA first numerical search used the determinant of affine fibre coordinates. It returned spurious zeros at branch points, where two fibre points coincide. Dividing by the Vandermonde of a linear form removes them, but only if the form is not constant on a collinear fibre: \(Y\) fails on the fibre over \(O\). The exact computation above does not depend on any such normalization.

86. The Riemann–Roch shape, and exact elimination over \(\mathbb Q\)

Fix \(P\in C(k)\) and a frame \((L,H,Z)\) with \(P=(0{:}0{:}1)\), \(H\) tangent at \(P\) and \(L\) another line through \(P\). For unknowns \(s,b_0,c_0\), put \(L'=L+sH\) and \(Z'=Z+b_0L+c_0H\). Let \(G(z,t)=t^{-2}F(-t,-t^2,z)\), computed in the frame \((L',H,Z')\), be the residual sextic of the pencil \(HZ'+zL'^2\). The monomial count \(L'^iH^jZ'^k\mapsto t^{i+2j-2}z^k\) gives \(\deg_zg_k\le(3,2,2,1,1,0,0)\) for \(k=0,\dots,6\). The leading coefficient \(g_6\) is the value of \(F\) at the point \(\ell\cap N_0\), so \(g_6\ne0\) exactly when that point is off the curve.

Theorem 86.1(Shape theorem.) The pencil \(HZ'+zL'^2\) is the pencil of fibres of \(x_Q\circ f\), for a degree-3 morphism \(f:C\to E\) with \(f^*Q=\ell\cdot C-P\), if and only if three conditions hold. First, \(g_6\ne0\). Second, \[ G(z,t)=g_6\big(S(z,t)^2-\kappa(z)\big),\qquad S=t^3+e_2t^2+(e_1+f_1z)\,t+(e_0+f_0z), \] with constants \(e_2,e_1,f_1,e_0,f_0\) and a separable cubic \(\kappa\). Third, \(G(z_0,t)\) is irreducible for some \(z_0\). The target is then \(E:w^2=\kappa(z)\), with \(w=S\).

The proof of necessity is as follows. Here \(\operatorname{div}(H/\ell)=P+r_1+r_2-f^*Q\), so \(t=H/L'\in L(f^*Q)\). The elementary symmetric functions of \(t\) over the fibres of \(f\) therefore lie in \(L(Q)=\langle1\rangle\), \(L(2Q)=\langle1,x\rangle\) and \(L(3Q)=\langle1,x,y\rangle\) on \(E\). Since \(z=\alpha x+\beta\), the minimal polynomial of \(t\) over \(k(E)\) is \(S+cy\), where \(S\) has the stated shape and \(c\ne0\), because \(t\notin k(z)\). Its norm to \(k(z)\) is \(S^2-c^2y^2\). This norm is the minimal polynomial \(G/g_6\) of \(t\), since \(k(C)=k(z,t)\): the point is \([-t:-t^2:z]\). For sufficiency, \(w=S\) satisfies \(w^2=\kappa(z)\) on \(C\). Irreducibility gives \([k(C):k(z)]=6\), and a separable cubic gives \([k(z,w):k(z)]=2\) and genus 1. So the map has degree 3.

This sharpens §82. The square completion (82.3) is not merely sufficient but necessary. Necessity also forces \(e_2\) to be constant and the two lower coefficients to be affine in \(z\). On \(C^\star\), \(S=t^3+9t^2-3zt-9z-27\) has exactly this form.

Derived(The system.) The coefficients of \(t^5,t^4,t^3\) determine \(e_2,e_1,f_1,e_0,f_0\) linearly once \(w=1/g_6\) is adjoined. The coefficients of \(t^2\) and \(t^1\) then give six polynomial equations in \((w,s,b_0,c_0)\), three \(z\)-coefficients each. Adding \(wg_6-1\) gives seven equations. This chart (I) covers every collinear fibre whose line \(\ell\) is not the tangent at \(P\). Each pair \((f,Q)\) with \(P_Q=P\) gives exactly one solution: \(\ell\) is determined, and \(N_0\) is the unique member through \(H\). The remaining case is \(\ell=H\), where the collinear fibre lies on the tangent and contains \(P\). It is chart II: the pencil \(HZ+aL^2+bLH+zH^2\) with \(t'=L/H\in L(f^*Q)\), to which the same shape theorem applies (chart2.py). No prime, no splitting of contact points, no Hensel precision and no rational reconstruction enter anywhere.

ScopeWhat is certified needs stating exactly. The solver uses Singular's modStd with its final test switched on. That test proves \(I\subseteq\langle G\rangle\) and that \(G\) is a Gröbner basis. So every computed solution is a solution, and each one is re-verified in any case by the exact map identity. It does not prove \(V(I)\subseteq V(G)\): a returned basis \(\{1\}\) certifies nothing on its own. I tried three ways of closing this gap. Exact std over \(\mathbb Q\) did not finish within 23 minutes at \(P_1\), nor within 15 minutes on the inconsistent system at \(R\). The single-prime degree bound for finite \(\mathbb Z_{(p)}\)-schemes is not available either: the homogenized system modulo 32003 has two-dimensional components at infinity (affine-cone dimension 3, multiplicity 6 there). For \(C^\star\), completeness follows from theory instead.

Derived(Corollary 86.2.) By §73, \(\operatorname{Jac}C^\star\sim E\times A\) with \(A\) absolutely simple, and \(f\) is optimal because its degree is prime. So every degree-3 morphism \(C^\star\to E'\) over \(\overline{\mathbb Q}\) is \(\alpha\circ f\) for an isomorphism \(\alpha\), and has the same fibres as \(f\). By Theorem 85.1 and Corollary 85.2, over \(\overline{\mathbb Q}\) there is exactly one elliptic pencil at \(P_1\), exactly one at \(P_2\), and none at any other point of \(C^\star\), in either chart. In particular there is none at \(R\).

MeasuredIn every frame the solver returns exactly what Corollary 86.2 predicts: one pencil at each of the two base points and none at the third rational point. At \(R\), Part XIX's engine, given 12 primes up to 83, returns nothing after 31 s, which is not a certificate. At \(P_2\) that engine does find the pencil, at \(p=17\), once \(P_2\) is supplied. The second base point is therefore not a case Part XIX cannot handle. It is a case Part XIX did not know to look for, and the theorem of §85 is what supplies it. Chart II returns no solution at \(P_1\), \(P_2\) or \(R\). This agrees with the theory, because the lines \(Y=0\) and \(Z=0\) are not tangent at their base points. Chart II has not yet been tested on a curve where it has a solution.

Measured(family_basepoints.py.) The same test was run on the seven family classes other than \(C^\star\), at every rational point of height at most 10, which gives 18 points in all. Each class has exactly two base points among them, \((1{:}0{:}1)\) and \((3w{:}-1{:}0)\). Each base point carries exactly one pencil, to the expected target. The other four rational points, two on \((1,-2)\) and two on \((1,4)\), have none. This matches Theorem 85.1. For these curves, though, the uniqueness of the elliptic subcover is not proved here, so the zero counts are computed results, not theorems.

Negative resultI also tried to remove the base point as an input altogether, by making it an unknown \((p,q)\) on the curve with \(F_X(p,q,1)\ne0\) (freeP.lib). The Gröbner computation modulo 32003 did not finish in 15 minutes. Eliminating the base point is not yet feasible in this formulation.

88. Status after Part XX

Part XIX's identities, map and checker are confirmed by code that imports nothing from it. Two of its counts are corrected: six contact solutions at 17, not eight, and eight distinct benchmark curves, one of them \(C^\star\), not nine unrelated members plus \(C^\star\). The base point is no longer an arbitrary input. Every degree-3 elliptic subcover of a smooth plane quartic has exactly two collinear fibres, and their residual points are the only places the construction can work. On \(C^\star\) these are \(P_1\) and \(P_2=(-3{:}1{:}0)\), and the pushforward law \(f(P_Q)\oplus[3]Q=(7,-9)\) holds at both. Square completion with affine lower coefficients is now proved necessary as well as sufficient. That turns pencil discovery at a given point into seven exact polynomial equations in four unknowns, solved in 3–8 s with no prime, splitting condition or Hensel precision. On \(C^\star\), the count of one pencil at each base point and none elsewhere is a theorem, and the solver reproduces it in all 13 frames tested. On the seven other family classes it finds exactly two rational base points each.

Four items remain open. First, completeness of the solver without theory. The verified modular basis proves soundness but not completeness, and exact Gröbner bases over \(\mathbb Q\) did not terminate within 15–23 minutes. The natural fix is a Nullstellensatz certificate, \(1=\sum c_if_i\) with cofactors reconstructed multimodularly and checked exactly. For the positive cases, the analogue expresses each element of the computed basis in terms of the input. Second, quadratic base points. When \(Q_1,Q_2\) are conjugate, \(P_{Q_i}\) is defined over a quadratic field and the same system must be solved over that field. The benchmark family has rational base points by construction, so a curve with conjugate collinear fibres is the next test case. Third, removing the base point as an input. The formulation with \(P\) unknown is too heavy, and a lower-dimensional one should parametrize lines \(\ell\in\mathbb P^{2\vee}\) and impose that three of the four points of \(\ell\cdot C\) form a fibre. Fourth, a positive test of chart II, on a quartic whose collinear fibre lies on a tangent line.

Reproducibility. The four scripts ec_crest.py, root_crest.py, height_crest.py and sym_crest.py, with their JSON outputs, are in the accompanying archive. They use PARI/GP 2.17 through cypari2, together with NumPy and SymPy. Part II adds cert_crest.py for the Arb-certified window statistics and budget, twist_D.py for the bracketed \(\mathfrak D_E\) over the twist family, and sq_check.py for the prime-square transient, with outputs cert_all.json, twist_D.jsonl and twist_fit.json. The ten certified runs took about 80 minutes on 2 cores, almost all of it computing \(a_p\). Part IV adds eoe_test2.py and eoe_test3.py for the excised-ensemble simulations and bootstrap tests, plus arith_split.py and arith_predict.py for the small-prime analysis. Their outputs are eoe_final.json, eoe_2param.json and arith_predict.json. Part III adds twist_resid.py for the zero-subdivision cross-check and the residual analysis, with output twist_zeros_fine.json. It also corrects height_crest.py to \(4\varphi(h)\) and makes root_crest.py use exact integer convolution. The first-edition FFT outputs are kept as root_results_fft.json. Scope. This is an additive independent research result based on the Part XX archive. It closes the missing positive example for the tangent-line (chart-II) branch; proves absolute completeness of that chart for a new infinite family without modular Gröbner computation; and constructs a linearly disjoint tower of cubic covers with exact, compressed finite-field point counts. It does not claim a base-point-free algorithm for arbitrary plane quartics or solve the general Nullstellensatz cofactor problem in Part XX.

89. A rational family of genus-three elliptic subcovers

For a rational parameter m, let C_m be the projective plane curve F_m(X,Y,Z)=0, where

\[ F_m=-X^4-3X^2Z^2-4YZ^3-2X^2YZ+X^2Y^2-Y^2Z^2+Y^3Z-mY^4. \]

Let P=(0:0:1). The tangent line is Y=0 and its intersection divisor is

\[ (Y=0)\cdot C_m=2P+R_++R_-,\qquad R_\pm=(\pm\sqrt{-3}:0:1). \]

The rational functions

\[ u=4(X^2+YZ)/Y^2,\qquad v=4(2X^3+3XYZ)/Y^3 \]

satisfy the homogeneous polynomial identity

\[ Y^6\{v^2-u^3-u^2+4u-16m\}=16Y^2F_m. \]

Thus f_m=(u,v) extends to a nonconstant morphism C_m -> E_m with

\[ E_m:v^2=u^3+u^2-4u+16m. \]

It has degree three. Put z=-u/4, w=-v/4, and t=X/Y. The function-field presentation is

\[ w^2=-4z^3+z^2+z+m,\qquad t^3+3zt=w. \]

Over Q(z), a specialization at z=1 of the degree-six polynomial for t at m=1 is t^6+6t^4+9t^2+1, irreducible modulo 7. For the full family, a pole-divisor argument establishes deg(z:C_m -> P^1)=6 whenever the quartic is smooth; since E_m -> P^1_z has degree two, the morphism f_m has degree three.

For smoothness, in the chart Y=1 write

\[ h_m(x,z)=-x^4-3x^2z^2-4z^3-2x^2z+x^2-z^2+z-m. \]

The derivative in x equals -2x(2x^2+3z^2+2z-1). In the branch x=0, eliminating z from h_m=h_{m,z}=0 yields a nonzero multiple of 432m^2+76m-17. In the other branch, substituting x^2=(1-3z^2-2z)/2 yields a resultant proportional to (4m-1)(432m^2+76m-17). The curve is smooth on Y=0 for all m. The discriminant of the quadratic 432m^2+76m-17 is 16*13^3, which is not a square in Q. Therefore every rational m other than 1/4 gives a smooth genus-three quartic. At m=1/4, the points Y=1, Z=0, X^2=1/2 are singular. The elliptic cubic discriminant is -16(432m^2+76m-17), so all rational members have a nonsingular target. Its j-invariant is

\[ j(E_m)=-35152/(432m^2+76m-17). \]

This nonconstant rational function produces infinitely many distinct elliptic targets.

90. Exact completeness in the previously untested tangent chart

Consider a tangent conic pencil at P, in the natural projective frame,

\[ YZ+aX^2+bXY+zY^2=0,\qquad a\ne0. \]

Write T=X/Y, so Z/Y=-(aT^2+bT+z). Substitute into the quartic and let

\[ G(T,z)=F_m(T,1,-aT^2-bT-z)=\sum_{k=0}^6 g_k(z)T^k. \]

A degree-three elliptic factor in the Riemann–Roch shape of Part XX requires

\[ G/g_6=\left[T^3+e_2T^2+(e_1+f_1z)T+(e_0+f_0z)\right]^2-\kappa(z), \]

with deg(kappa)=3, g_6 ne 0. The top coefficients yield g_6=a^2(4a-3), g_5=6ab(2a-1), [z]g_4=6a(2a-1), [z]g_3=2b(12a-3), [z^2]g_2=12a-3, and [z^2]g_1=12b. The coefficient of z^2 T^2 in the square condition gives the necessary polynomial equation

\[ A(a,b)=4g_6[z^2]g_2-([z]g_4)^2=48a^3(a-1)=0. \]

The coefficient of z^2 T gives

\[ B(a,b)=4g_6^2[z^2]g_1-2g_6([z]g_4)([z]g_3)+g_5([z]g_4)^2 =48a^4b(4a^2-6a+3)=0. \]

Because a ne 0 and g_6 ne 0, the first equation forces a=1. The second becomes 48b=0 and forces b=0. Substitution shows that the remaining conditions hold identically, with

\[ G(T,z)=(T^3+3zT)^2-(-4z^3+z^2+z+m). \]

The tangent chart has exactly one solution over the algebraic closure in characteristic zero, for every smooth rational parameter. This completeness proof uses two explicit low-degree identities; no approximate modular basis, height search, or unverified cofactor is involved. It settles chart-II completeness for this family, not for arbitrary quartics.

The line Y=0 is itself a complete fibre plus the residual point P. On the affine base E_m - {O}, the monogenic cubic algebra with basis {1,t,t^2} is finite free of rank three. In this basis, the three canonical plane sections {Y,X,Z} become {1,t,-t^2-z}, an invertible change of basis. Hence the canonical evaluation determinant does not vanish at any finite point of E_m. Since the determinant has degree two (Part XX, §85), its complete zero divisor is 2[O]. The two collinear fibres counted with multiplicity therefore coincide, a degeneracy missing from the earlier benchmark cases.

91. Arithmetic inverse design without changing the map construction

The elliptic trace of E_m at an odd good prime p is exactly

\[ a_p(E_m)=-\sum_{x\in\mathbf F_p}\chi_p(x^3+x^2-4x+16m). \]

This depends only on m modulo p. A finite-prime specification can therefore be realized by selecting a permitted residue of m at each prime and applying the Chinese remainder theorem. This is a mathematically valid local inverse design; it does not prescribe global rank or full genus-three zeta polynomials. An exhaustive residue optimization for p=5,7,11,13 selected

\[ m\equiv0\pmod5,\quad m\equiv0\pmod7,\quad m\equiv0\pmod{11},\quad m\equiv6\pmod{13}, \]

with the smallest-magnitude solution m=1540 modulo 5005. The corresponding exact elliptic traces are -2,-2,-6,-7 and point counts are 8,10,18,21. The genus-three curve has 8,14,24,23 rational points at those primes. Good reduction was checked in each case. The map to the elliptic quotient is the same explicit formula for all m.

92. Independent nonabelian cubic-cover tower

Fix m=1 and let E:w^2=-4z^3+z^2+z+1. For integers i=0,...,n-1 define cubic extensions of its function field by

\[ t_i^3+3(z+i)t_i=w. \]

Their discriminants are -27 D_i(z), where

\[ D_i(z)=(12i+1)z^2+(12i^2+1)z+(4i^3+1). \]

For 0 <= i < 10, all D_i have distinct roots; none shares a root with the elliptic cubic; and every pair D_i,D_j is coprime. These assertions are verified by exact integer discriminants and 45 exact pairwise resultants. Each cubic is geometrically irreducible: a function-field root would have no poles away from O, and valuations at O force a pole of order exactly one, impossible on an elliptic curve by Riemann–Roch. Each Galois closure has group S_3 because the discriminant has four simple zeros. Their unique branch divisors ensure that the closures are linearly disjoint; hence the normalized fibre product X_n is geometrically connected and degree 3^n over E.

Each cubic subcover has four simple branch points on E. Riemann–Hurwitz for the fibre product therefore gives

\[ 2g(X_n)-2=4n3^{n-1},\qquad g(X_n)=1+2n3^{n-1}. \]

At n=10 this is a curve of genus 393661, with degree 59049 over the elliptic base. This is a genuine highly structured curve, not a generic high-genus point-count algorithm.

At a prime p>3 of simultaneous good reduction, let N_i(z,w) be the number of roots over F_p of the i-th cubic. The fibre above the elliptic origin has 2+chi_p(-3(12i+1)) rational points on the i-th cover. Thus

\[ \#X_n(\mathbf F_p)= \sum_{(z,w)\in E(\mathbf F_p)\setminus\{O\}}\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}N_i(z,w) +\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}(2+\chi_p(-3(12i+1))). \]

A finite-field implementation uses a table of N_i values and takes polynomial rather than exponential effort in n for fixed p. For n=10, the complete rational point counts at p=41,53,59,71 are respectively 81,2268,2952,243. All four primes were separately tested for simultaneous smooth good reduction. The single-cover formula was independently compared with direct projective point enumeration for each of the ten quartics at all four primes, and the two-cover case was checked by direct tuple enumeration.

Limitations and provenance. The arithmetic building blocks (Riemann–Hurwitz, Galois groups of cubics, CRT, Riemann–Roch, conic/contact incidence) are established mathematics. What is added is a constructive tangent-chart family with an elementary absolute completeness proof and a scalable independent cubic-cover engine integrated with the existing Root–Crest inverse geometry approach. The general height-free chart-I completeness problem, nonrational residual-base-point discovery, and automatic global correspondence search outside structured families remain open.

94. Four routes that do not produce certificates

Negative resultThe obvious constructions all fail, and each failure is measured.

Exact Gröbner bases over \(\mathbb Q\) did not finish. The four-variable system of §86 ran past 23 minutes at \(P_1\) and 15 minutes at \(R\). The three-variable form of §95 ran past 26 minutes at both points.

Multimodular reconstruction of Singular's lift output does not converge. At \(R\), the mod-\(p\) certificates of \(1\in I\) have 40,182 terms of degree at most 29, and their supports agree across two primes in all but 3 terms. Yet about 15,800 coefficients fail rational reconstruction at every modulus from 62 to 682 bits, and the count fluctuates instead of falling. A cofactor vector is determined only up to syzygies of \(I\), and the per-prime computations land on different representatives. The lifts are incoherent.

Canonicalizing by normal forms modulo the syzygy module failed on cost: the module Gröbner basis took more than 10 minutes mod \(p\).

Canonical linear algebra over the full monomial basis gives a 6,415 × 3,185 system per prime. Its RREF solution with free variables set to zero is coherent, but its heights are Cramer-sized. A restricted version on the original scaling still had 1,593 of 1,778 coefficients unreconstructed at 3,968 bits.

95. Certificates that work, and what they prove

Current-edition correction. Subsequent update: §98 contains an independent end-to-end re-derivation of all generators and four cofactor identities; §101 supplies a global geometric exclusion of chart II on C⋆.

Derived(Reformulation.) Solving the linear auxiliaries \(e_2,e_1,f_1,e_0,f_0\) of Theorem 86.1 over \(\mathbb Q(s,b_0,c_0)\) and clearing powers of \(g_6\) replaces the seven equations in \((w,s,b_0,c_0)\) by six equations \(r_1,\dots,r_6\) in \((s,b_0,c_0)\), of degrees 20, 20, 20, 25, 25 and 25. Write \(I_0\) for the ideal they generate. Every solution of the §86 system satisfies \(g_6\ne0\) and solves \(I_0\). Conversely, every solution of \(I_0\) with \(g_6\ne0\) solves the §86 system. So the pencils at \(P\) are exactly \(V(I_0)\setminus V(g_6)\). Modulo a prime, \(I_0\) has a Gröbner basis in about 1 s. It shows \(g_6^2\in I_0\) at \(R\), and \(s\,g_6^2,\ b_0g_6^2,\ c_0g_6^2\in I_0\) at \(P_1\).

Measured(Rescaling.) The \(3\)-adic valuation of the coefficient of \(s^{i}b_0^{j}c_0^{k}\) is, by least squares, close to \(4i+0.8j+4.8k\) plus a constant, and the \(2\)-adic valuation close to \(i+k\). These are the denominators that actually occur, for example \(c_0=-\tfrac1{54}\) at \(P_2\) and \(s=\tfrac1{27}\) in the transformed frames. Substituting \(s=S/162\), \(b_0=B/3\), \(c_0=C/486\) and removing contents cuts the largest coefficients from 143–180 bits to 36–52 bits. The substitution is invertible, so it changes no zero set.

Measured(Support-restricted canonical solve.) The unknowns are the 1,898 monomials of the mod-\(p\) Gröbner lift. The restricted system has rank 1,778 at every prime tested, with identical pivot sets. Its RREF solution with free variables set to zero is therefore canonical, and it is reconstructed from 62-bit primes until two successive reconstructions agree. The certificate is then rebuilt and checked exactly by check_cert.py and check_R_cert.py. These start again from the quartic, re-derive \(r_1,\dots,r_6\) and \(g_6\), apply the rescaling, and verify the polynomial identity in python-flint, trusting no Singular output.

Theorem 95.1(Certified computation.) On \(C^\star\), no elliptic pencil in chart I has base point \(R=(3{:}1{:}0)\). At \(P_1=(1{:}0{:}1)\), the pencil \(HZ+zL^2\) of Part XIX is the only chart-I pencil. Both statements hold over \(\overline{\mathbb Q}\). The proof is as follows. At \(R\), \(g_6^2\in I_0\), so \(g_6\) vanishes at every common zero of \(I_0\), and \(V(I_0)\setminus V(g_6)=\varnothing\). At \(P_1\), \(S\,g_6^2,\ B\,g_6^2,\ C\,g_6^2\in I_0\), so every common zero with \(g_6\ne0\) has \(S=B=C=0\). That point is the verified pencil of §82. Unlike Corollary 86.2, this argument uses nothing about \(\operatorname{End}(\operatorname{Jac}C^\star)\). What it does use is the shape theorem of §86 and four polynomial identities that anyone can recheck.

ScopeThis closes G01 for chart I at two points of one curve. It does not yet cover chart II, which needs the same treatment of its own system, or the second base point \(P_2\). Nor is it an automatic pipeline. Each certificate needed one Singular lift modulo a small prime, for the support, and about 4–5 minutes of multimodular linear algebra on 2 cores. The rescaling exponents were fitted by hand and are essential: without them the same run had not converged at 3,968 bits. Neither G02 (quadratic base points) nor G03 (base-point elimination) is advanced here. Two of the next steps are mechanical: certificates for chart II at \(P_1\), \(P_2\) and \(R\), and the \(P_2\) uniqueness certificate. Two need new ideas: choosing the rescaling automatically from valuations, and turning the per-point certificates into the "no map with a rational collinear fibre" statement for every rational point of bounded height, beginning with the family curves of §87.

96. Reconciliation of Parts XXI and XXII, with provenance and limitations

The canonical monograph previously ended at §88. Part XXI (§§89–92) existed in a separate 1,461-entry archive; Part XXII (§§93–95) existed in a 1,494-entry archive containing the older 1,447-entry base but missing the fourteen Part XXI files. The common members of the two source archives are byte-identical, including the prior crest/index.html. The current integration incorporates the fourteen Part XXI research files and the forty-seven Part XXII research files into one canonical tree; the historical monograph remains available as index_before_part_xxiii.html.

We distinguish mathematical statements proved by general algebra from conditional conclusions based on previous claims about the geometric endomorphism algebra of the reference quartic, and from computational certificates. The integral-cofactor calculations below verify the actual archived ideal membership identities from scratch, using no Singular or FLINT. A separate polynomial-ring computation re-derives the generators directly from the defining quartic. This avoids treating an exported Gröbner basis as the source of the theorem.

The relevant reference curve is the smooth plane quartic

\[ C^\star:\quad F=X^4-6X^3Y+2X^3Z-27X^2Y^2-18X^2YZ-3X^2Z^2+54XY^3-31XZ^3+162Y^4+108Y^3Z+837Y^2Z^2+186YZ^3+31Z^4=0. \]

The three reference rational points are \(P_1=(1:0:1)\), \(P_2=(-3:1:0)\), and \(R=(3:1:0)\). Statements about chart completeness at \(P_1\) and \(R\) refer to the exact shape theorem of §86, including nonvanishing \(g_6\). The rational \(P_2\) map was previously constructed, but its independent chart-I cofactor identity has not yet been generated. The global elliptic-factor argument of §73 gives a separate geometric uniqueness statement for \(C^\star\), subject to the published geometric-simplicity calculation.

97. Low-height reconstruction of the chart-I elimination ideal

Write the chart-I residual sextic as

\[ G(z,t)=\sum_{j=0}^6g_j(z)t^j,\qquad g_6\ne0. \]

The Riemann–Roch shape theorem requires

\[ G=g_6\{S^2-\kappa(z)\},\qquad S=t^3+e_2t^2+(e_1+f_1z)t+(e_0+f_0z). \]

Here \(\kappa\) is a separable cubic and the five auxiliary coefficients are determined by \(g_6,g_5,g_4,g_3\). Write \(g_{jk}=[z^k]g_j\), and define polynomials in the three chart variables \(s,b,c\) by

\[ \begin{aligned} a&=g_5,\\ b_0&=4g_{40}g_6-a^2, & b_1&=g_{41},\\ c_0&=8g_{30}g_6^2-ab_0, &c_1&=2g_{31}g_6-ab_1,\\ d_1(z)&=b_0+4b_1g_6z, &d_0(z)&=c_0+4c_1g_6z. \end{aligned} \]

(The subscripts \(b_0,c_0\) in these expressions denote intermediate polynomial numerators, not the names of the chart variables; the executable uses capitalized local names to avoid ambiguity.) Then

\[ e_2=\frac a{2g_6},\qquad e_1+f_1z=\frac{d_1(z)}{8g_6^2},\qquad e_0+f_0z=\frac{d_0(z)}{16g_6^3}. \]

The six generators of the saturated chart-I system, before primitive-content normalization, are precisely the three coefficients in \(z\) of each polynomial

\[ \boxed{N_2(z)=64g_2(z)g_6^3-d_1(z)^2-4a\,d_0(z),} \]
\[ \boxed{N_1(z)=64g_1(z)g_6^4-d_1(z)d_0(z).} \]

No rational-function simplification is required to calculate these generators. They arise by clearing the exact common denominators of the two remaining coefficients of \(S^2-G/g_6\); the restriction \(g_6\ne0\) is retained throughout. A sparse polynomial-ring implementation substitutes the quartic into the contact frame, extracts \(g_j\), builds \(N_1,N_2\), and rescales the three variables. For both \(P_1\) and \(R\), all six rescaled generators and \(g_6\) match the archived Part XXII generators up to their primitive scalar normalization: fourteen out of fourteen independent symbolic comparisons succeed. The computation requires about 0.2 s per point in this environment, in contrast with the slow old SymPy together route.

98. Full exact proof-chain verification without Singular or FLINT

For \(P_1\), Part XXII supplies rational-cofactor families witnessing

\[ Sg_6^2=\sum_{j=1}^6U_jN_j,\quad Bg_6^2=\sum_{j=1}^6V_jN_j,\quad Cg_6^2=\sum_{j=1}^6W_jN_j. \]

For \(R\), it supplies \(g_6^2=\sum_{j=1}^6T_jN_j\). Thus every chart-I solution at \(P_1\) with \(g_6\ne0\) has \(S=B=C=0\), while no such solution exists at \(R\). The unique remaining solution at \(P_1\) is the explicitly checked degree-three map to \(E:V^2=U^3-29U-59\).

We implemented an independent verifier using integer dictionaries indexed by exponent triples. Each rational cofactor is represented over the common denominator \(D=\mathrm{lcm}\{\mathrm{den}(c)\}\). The program compares, coefficient-by-coefficient in \(\mathbb Z[S,B,C]\),

\[ D\sum_jU_jN_j-D\,Sg_6^2 \]

and the three analogous expressions. Each resulting polynomial is exactly zero, across approximately 3,600 monomial positions. The four cofactors contain 1,778, 1,777, 1,777 and 1,777 terms respectively. The verifier rejects a deliberately altered cofactor as a negative control. The proof chain is therefore: quartic equation \(\to\) independent elimination generators \(\to\) exact rational-cofactor identities \(\to\) chart-I uniqueness or impossibility. This is stronger than merely rerunning Singular's output parser, but still relies on the established Riemann–Roch shape theorem and the attached, trusted source archive.

99. Automatically selecting p-adic polynomial rescalings

Part XXII's cofactor-generation procedure required a hand-chosen substitution \((s,b,c)=(S/162,B/3,C/486)\). We designed a bounded automatic precursor. For each small prime \(p\) and exponent vector \(\mathbf k=(k_1,k_2,k_3)\), it measures the spread of corrected valuations

\[ \omega_p(F;\mathbf k)= \max_{\mathbf e}\bigl(v_p(c_{\mathbf e})-\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf e\bigr) - \min_{\mathbf e}\bigl(v_p(c_{\mathbf e})-\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf e\bigr). \]

The coefficients \(c_{\mathbf e}\) are the nonzero integer coefficients of an eliminated generator, and \(\mathbf e\) is its exponent triple. Candidate exponent vectors minimizing the spreads for \(p=2,3\) are combined and evaluated by actual bit lengths after clearing denominators and removing primitive content. In 100 deterministic candidate combinations drawn from the two reference systems, the optimal tested common substitution was

\[ \boxed{(s,b,c)=(S/162,B,C/162).} \]

For \(P_1\), the largest primitive generator coefficient shrinks from 130 bits with no rescaling and 49 bits under Part XXII's hand-chosen rescaling to 30 bits. For \(R\), the corresponding figures are 159, 52 and 46 bits. All rescalings are invertible and preserve the relevant rational zero sets. This is a genuine, measured reduction in the input coefficient heights. It does not yet prove a reduction in the heights of subsequent cofactors or their total generation time; neither has been re-run under the new choice. It is a bounded tropical-style search rather than a proof of globally minimal scaling.

100. An infinite family of linearly disjoint nonabelian cubic covers

Part XXI proved disjointness for \(i=0,\ldots,9\). The same phenomenon can be proved for all nonnegative integers \(i\). Let

\[ E:w^2=-4z^3+z^2+z+1, \qquad h_i(T)=T^3+3(z+i)T-w, \]

and let \(K_i/K(E)\) be the extension obtained by adjoining a root of \(h_i\). The cubic discriminant is \(-27D_i(z)\), with

\[ D_i(z)=(12i+1)z^2+(12i^2+1)z+(4i^3+1). \]

Theorem 100.1 (Infinite disjoint cubic tower). For every \(n\ge1\), the extensions \(K_0,\ldots,K_{n-1}\) are geometrically linearly disjoint; their Galois closures have group \(S_3^n\). The smooth projective normalization \(X_n\) of their fibre product is geometrically connected of degree \(3^n\) over \(E\), with

\[ \boxed{g(X_n)=1+2n3^{n-1}.} \]

Proof. The discriminant of \(D_i\) as a quadratic in \(z\) is

\[ -48i^4-16i^3+24i^2-48i-3<0\qquad(i\ge0). \]

Two distinct real-coefficient quadratics with negative discriminants could share a root only if they were proportional. Their middle-to-leading coefficient ratio

\[ \rho_i=\frac{12i^2+1}{12i+1} \]

is strictly increasing for integers \(i\ge1\), since \(\rho'(x)=12(12x^2+2x-1)/(12x+1)^2>0\) for \(x\ge1\). The only tie is \(\rho_0=\rho_1=1\), but \(D_0=z^2+z+1\) and \(D_1=13z^2+13z+5\) are not proportional. Thus all the \(D_i\) have pairwise disjoint simple root sets. In addition,

\[ \operatorname{Res}_z(D_i,-4z^3+z^2+z+1) =16(4i^3+i^2-i+1)^3\ne0. \]

So each zero of \(D_i\) lifts to two distinct points of the elliptic base and is disjoint from the other branch loci. At the elliptic origin the local uniformizer \(\tau=z/w\) gives \(z=-1/(4\tau^2)+1/4+O(\tau^2)\). The cubic's leading sheet constants are \(-1,\frac12,\frac12\). On the two coincident leading sheets, write \(T=(2\tau)^{-1}+b+O(\tau)\). The coefficient of \(\tau^{-1}\) is \(\frac32b^2+\frac32i+\frac18\), giving \(b^2=-(12i+1)/12\ne0\), two distinct branches. Thus the origin is unramified on the normalized cover. The cubic has no global rational-function root: a root would be regular away from the elliptic origin and have a simple pole there, forbidden by Riemann–Roch on \(E\). Its nonsquare discriminant therefore gives Galois group \(S_3\). At each of its four branch points, inertia is a transposition, whose normal closure in \(S_3\) is all of \(S_3\). Since the branch supports of the different extensions are disjoint, each new Galois closure has trivial intersection with the compositum of the previous ones. Induction gives \(S_3^n\), and Riemann–Hurwitz yields \(2g(X_n)-2=4n3^{n-1}\). \(\square\)

The exact symbolic script independently checks the discriminants and resultants and the coefficient of the local Puiseux equation. The formula gives \(g(X_{20})=46,490,458,681\) and \(g(X_{100})=34,358,501,382,134,088,735,764,075,317,708,084,846,807,168,133,401\). No claim is made that the full zeta polynomials of these curves have been computed. For fixed \(p\), sufficiently many indices eventually coincide modulo \(p\), so one cannot fix a single good reduction prime for the entire infinite tower. Every point-counting computation must separately validate good reduction at its chosen finite stage.

101. A base-point-free fibre localization operation for known maps

Part XX's determinant theorem can be turned into a small exact algorithm once the elliptic map is known, avoiding enumeration of rational points just to locate the collinear fibres. For \(C^\star\), use the cubic function-field presentation

\[ t^3+9t^2-3zt-(w+9z+27)=0, \quad w^2=-27(z^3+27z^2-18z-27). \]

Write \(A=w+9z+27\). In \(K(E)[t]/(t^3+9t^2-3zt-A)\), one has \(t^{-1}=(t^2+9t-3z)/A\). The plane sections, after trivializing by \(Y\), are

\[ Y/Y=1,\qquad Z/Y=-z/t,\qquad X/Y=t+6-z/t. \]

Express these in the basis \(1,t,t^2\) and take their determinant:

\[ \boxed{\Delta(z,w)=\frac{z}{w+9z+27}.} \]

The identity \((9z+27)^2-w^2=27z^2(z+30)\) shows the divisor of this rationally trivialized determinant:

\[ \operatorname{div}(\Delta) =[O]+[(0,27)]-[(0,-27)]-[(-30,243)]. \]

The poles come from the choice of a rational basis; they are not additional collinear fibres. The determinant of the canonical evaluation map is a regular section of the degree-two bundle of §85. Its actual zero divisor is \([O]+[(0,27)]\), where \((0,27)\) corresponds to \((-3,-1)\) on \(V^2=U^3-29U-59\). Its residual points are \(P_1=(1:0:1)\) and \(P_2=(-3:1:0)\). The verified tangent lines are respectively \(X-6Y-Z=0\) and \(X+3Y+2Z=0\), distinct from the corresponding fibre lines \(Y=0\) and \(Z=0\). Combining this with the previously established uniqueness of the degree-three elliptic factor shows that chart II has no map on \(C^\star\), at any residual point, not just the three tested rational points. This latter conclusion invokes the geometric uniqueness theorem of §73; it is not a new Nullstellensatz certificate for the chart-II polynomial ideal.

A genuine base-point-free discovery algorithm remains open: the determinant procedure needs the cubic cover and the map in advance. But it provides a generic intermediate module: given a cubic extension and canonical sections, determine its entire collinear-fibre divisor directly by arithmetic in the cubic algebra, including irreducible quadratic basepoint divisors when they occur.

Part XXIV. Where the collinear fibres are

103. Part XXIII, checked

In an isolated copy of the 1,537-entry release, all of Part XXIII's scripts pass: proof_chain.py, infinite_cubic_tower.py, fibre_determinant.py, optimize_scaling.py and its test suite. Part XXI's 12 tests also pass. All 1,438 files of the Part XXII tree are present byte for byte. The only changed file is index.html, whose old bytes are kept, as stated.

MeasuredI re-derived the cubic-tower theorem with my own code, independent of infinite_cubic_tower.py. The cubic \(t^3+3(z+i)t-w\) has discriminant \(-27(4(z+i)^3+w^2)=-27D_i(z)\) on \(E\). The discriminant of \(D_i\), the resultant \(16(4i^3+i^2-i+1)^3\), and the absence of proportional pairs for \(0\le i<j<60\) all reproduce. The scope \(i\ge0\) stated in §§98–99 is necessary: \(i=-1\) gives \(\operatorname{disc}D_{-1}=37>0\), and it is the only index in \([-50,50]\) with real roots. Singular's normalization (genus.sing) gives genus 3 for the single covers \(i=0,1,2\). It shows the fibre product of the covers for \(i=0\) and \(i=1\) is a single component over \(\mathbb Q\), of genus 13, which equals \(1+2n3^{n-1}\) at \(n=2\). This is a computation independent of the inertia argument.

A parity argument makes the absence of ramification over \(O\) explicit. With \(t=u/\pi\), the cubic in \(u\) has discriminant of valuation \(2\) at \(O\), because \(D_i\) has degree 2 in \(z\). The discriminant of a degree-3 order has the valuation of the maximal order's discriminant plus twice the index. A ramified point with one simple sheet contributes 1, which is odd. So the cover is unramified at \(O\), and the order has index 1 there.

104. Collinear fibres are W-models, and their sum is fixed by the branch divisor

Theorem 104.1Let \(f:C\to E\) be a degree-3 map from a smooth plane quartic, and let \(Q\in E(\bar k)\). Then \(f^*Q\) is collinear if and only if \(h^0(f^*Q)=2\). That in turn holds if and only if there is a function \(W\) with polar divisor exactly \(f^*Q\). Normalized to trace zero, such a \(W\) satisfies \(W^3+\alpha W+\beta=0\) with \(\alpha\in L(2Q)\) and \(\beta\in L(3Q)\). Call this a W-model at \(Q\). The proof is as follows. Riemann–Roch gives \(h^0(D)=1+h^0(K-D)\) for an effective divisor \(D\) of degree 3, and \(K-D\) has degree 1, so it is effective exactly when \(D\) is collinear. The symmetric functions of \(W\) over the fibres lie in \(L(Q)\), \(L(2Q)\) and \(L(3Q)\), as in Theorem 86.1. Conversely, in a W-model, \(W\) has degree 3 with poles only over \(Q\). This also shows that \(C\) is not hyperelliptic, since \(|f^*Q|\) has no base point.

Theorem 104.2(Branch-sum law.) The collinearity divisor satisfies \(\mathcal O_E(Q_1+Q_2)\cong(\det f_*\mathcal O_C)^{-1}\). Hence \(2(Q_1+Q_2)\sim B\), where \(B\) is the branch divisor, and in the group law \([2](Q_1\oplus Q_2)=\oplus B\). The proof is as follows. For a canonical curve, \(\mathcal O_C(1)=\omega_C\), and duality gives \(f_*\omega_C\cong(f_*\mathcal O_C)^\vee\otimes\omega_E\), with \(\omega_E\) trivial. The determinant section of §85 therefore lives in \((\det f_*\mathcal O_C)^{-1}\), while \((\det f_*\mathcal O_C)^{\otimes2}\cong\mathcal O(-B)\). In particular, if \(Q_1\) is rational then so is \(Q_2\). Every construction in which a W-model is built at a rational point therefore has rational second base point. This covers Part XVIII's family, Part XXI's family and the cubic tower.

105. The index point, and the second base point without search

Theorem 105.1(Index point.) Let \(W^3+\alpha W+\beta=0\) be a W-model at \(O\), and put \(\Delta=-4\alpha^3-27\beta^2\in L(6O)\). Then \[ \operatorname{div}(\Delta)+6O=B+2\,[\ominus Q_2], \] where \(Q_2\) is the second collinear fibre. The proof is as follows. Let \(M=\mathcal O_E\oplus\mathcal O_E(-O)W\oplus\mathcal O_E(-2O)W^2\). Then \(M\subseteq f_*\mathcal O_C\), because \(W\) has at most simple poles over \(O\), and \(\det M=\mathcal O(-3O)\). The index divisor \(N\) satisfies \(\det M=\det f_*\mathcal O_C\otimes\mathcal O(-N)\). Theorem 104.2 with \(Q_1=O\) gives \(\mathcal O(-3O)\cong\mathcal O(-O-Q_2-N)\), so the effective degree-1 divisor \(N\) is linearly equivalent to \(2O-Q_2\), and the only such divisor is the point \(\ominus Q_2\). Finally, the discriminant of \(M\) is that of \(f_*\mathcal O_C\) times the square of the index.

Measured(index_point.py, index_point_symbolic.json, branch_sum*.py.) For Part XVIII's family, \(W^3+UW+(c-V)=0\) on \(V^2=U^3+aU+b\) with \(a=2cw-31w^4\) and \(b=c^2+2cw^3-62w^6\). The restricted discriminant is divisible by \((V-(c-2w^3))^2\) identically in \((w,c)\), and the double point has \(U=-3w^2\). So \[ Q_2=(-3w^2,\ 2w^3-c)\qquad\text{for the whole two-parameter family,} \] in model coordinates. On each of the nine family runs, the remaining factor is an irreducible quartic of branch points, and \([2]Q_2=\oplus B\) holds to \(10^{-77}\). Examples are \(\oplus B=(7,9)\) for \(C^\star\) and \((63,217)\) for \((w,c)=(3,1)\). The model's \(V\) is the negative of the explicit map's \(V\) (§82), checked modulo the quartic. That is why §85 reports \(Q_2=(-3,-1)\) in map coordinates.

Derived(Corollary 105.2, the tower.) For \(t^3+3(z+i)t-w=0\), \(\Delta=-27D_i(z)\) has pole order only 4 at \(O\). So \(N=O\) and \(Q_2=O\). Every cover of the tower, for every \(i\ge0\), is a smooth plane quartic whose collinearity divisor is \(2[O]\). This gives a one-line explanation of the duplicated divisor that Part XXI found in its family.

Theorem 105.3(The second base point lies on \(N_0\).) Take the chart-I pencil \(HZ'+zL'^2\) at \(P_1\), with reducible member \(H\cdot N_0\). If \(Q_2\ne O\), then \(f^*Q_2\subset N_0\), \(P_2=N_0\cdot C-f^*Q_2\), and \(f(P_2)=-Q_2\). The proof is as follows. Every member of the pencil is a fibre pair \(2P_1+f^*R+f^*(-R)\), and three points of a smooth conic are never collinear. So a collinear fibre lies on a reducible member. These are \(\ell^2\), which belongs to \(O\), and \(H\cdot N_0\). The line \(H\) meets \(C\) in only two points besides \(2P_1\). So \(f^*Q_2\subset N_0\), and the rest of \(H\cdot N_0\) is \(r_1+r_2+P_2=f^*(-Q_2)\).

Measured(second_from_N0.py.) The second base point was computed from the single exact solution at \(P_1\), with no enumeration of rational points, on \(C^\star\) and on the seven other family classes. In every case \(N_0=Z\). On \(C^\star\), \(N_0\cdot C=(3{:}1{:}0)+(-3{:}1{:}0)+\{X^2-6XY-18Y^2=0\}\). On each of the other seven, it is one rational point plus an irreducible cubic, which is the conjugate triple \(f^*Q_2\). The rational point is \((-3w{:}1{:}0)=(3w{:}-1{:}0)\), exactly the second base point that §87 found by searching. Its image is \(-Q_2\) in every case. This answers the base-point half of G03 for curves that have one rational base point: the second is a byproduct of the first solve.

107. Status after Part XXIV

The two collinear fibres of a degree-3 elliptic subcover are now located by algebra. Theorem 104.2 ties their sum to the branch divisor. Theorem 105.1 finds the second one as the index point of the discriminant of a W-model at the first. Theorem 105.3 puts it on the line \(N_0\) of the solver's own output, so one solve yields both base points. For G02 the consequence is negative but sharp. A quadratic-conjugate pair can never come from a W-model built at a rational point, so the families of Parts XVIII, XXI and XXIII cannot supply one. A test curve must be a W-model at a point \(Q_1\in E(K)\setminus E(\mathbb Q)\) satisfying a descent condition: the second collinear fibre must be \(\sigma(Q_1)\), with conjugate W-model. Theorems 104.2 and 105.1 make that condition explicit, since \(Q_1\oplus\sigma(Q_1)\) must be a rational half of \(\oplus B\). Solving it is the next construction. For G03, the base-point search reduces to finding one base point, which remains a search over \(C(\mathbb Q)\) by height. G01 is complete for chart I on \(C^\star\) at its three rational points. The automatic pipeline and chart-II certificates remain open. Public deployment (P02) is still not done.
