Part XXV. Quadratic collinear fibres and Galois descent

108. Independent Part XXIV proof chain

Let \(C^\star\) denote the smooth quartic defined in §96. The Part XXIV chart-I ideal at \(P_2=(3:-1:0)\) has six generators \(r_1,\ldots,r_6\in\mathbb Z[s,b_0,c_0]\), with nonvanishing leading coefficient \(g_6\). Its recorded identities are

\[ Sg_6^2=\sum U_jr_j,\qquad (B-2)g_6^2=\sum V_jr_j,\qquad (C+1)g_6^2=\sum W_jr_j, \]

where the rescaling is \(s=S/54\), \(b_0=B\), \(c_0=C/54\). We re-derived the six primitive generators and \(g_6\) directly from the original plane quartic using the exact polynomial-ring shape equations in §97. All seven normalized polynomials match the archived \(P_2\) ideal. A separate verifier parses the human-readable cofactor polynomials; it never executes the archived pickle objects and does not import Singular or FLINT. After multiplying by the least common denominator, every integer coefficient of all three residual polynomials is zero. Each cofactor family has exactly 1,592 nonzero monomials, and each identity compares 3,385 monomial positions. This completes an independent exact verification of the archived chart-I system and its unique solution; the general shape theorem used to form that ideal is an explicit prerequisite.

109. The quadratic-base-point example

Let

\[ C_0:\quad X^3Y+Y^3Z+Z^3X=0, \]

and \(\sigma(X:Y:Z)=(Y:Z:X)\). This is the smooth Klein quartic, of genus three; \(\sigma\) has order three. The fixed points on \(C_0\) are exactly

\[ P_+=(1:\omega:\omega^2),\qquad P_-=(1:\omega^2:\omega),\quad \omega^2+\omega+1=0. \]

They are conjugate over \(K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})\). Riemann–Hurwitz gives \(2(3)-2=3(2g_E-2)+2(3-1)\), hence \(g_E=1\). The coordinate vertices form a rational orbit, so the quotient has a rational point. Define

\[ s_1=X+Y+Z,\quad s_2=XY+YZ+ZX,\quad s_3=XYZ,\quad u=s_2/s_1^2,\quad v=s_3/s_1^3. \]

Then the \(\sigma\)-invariant quotient is

\[ E_0:\ W^2=1-10u+27u^2-10u^3-27u^4, \qquad W=14v+u^2-5u+1. \]

The point \((u,W)=(0,1)\) is rational, giving an elliptic-curve origin. This map is degree three by the fixed-field theorem; no elliptic quotient was supplied to the calculation.

110. The collinear-fibre and bitangent identities

Write

\[ \ell_+=X+\omega Y+\omega^2Z,\qquad \ell_-=X+\omega^2Y+\omega Z. \]

Both are stable lines under the cyclic action. On \(C_0\), the line \(\ell_+\) cuts out \(P_++f^*Q_+\), and its conjugate cuts out \(P_-+f^*Q_-\). In particular \(f^*Q_\pm\) is a degree-three collinear fibre. Since

\[ \ell_+\ell_-=s_1^2-3s_2=s_1^2(1-3u), \]

both special fibres have \(u=1/3\). On \(E_0\), this gives

\[ Q_\pm=(1/3,\ \pm\sqrt{-3}/9). \]

Neither point nor its residual base point is \(\mathbb Q\)-rational. They are exchanged by the nontrivial element of \(\operatorname{Gal}(K/\mathbb Q)\). The remaining invariant line \(s_1=0\) satisfies the exact intersection identity

\[ C_0\big|_{Z=-X-Y}=-(X^2+XY+Y^2)^2. \]

Thus \(s_1=0\) is a rational bitangent meeting the quartic at the same two conjugate points, each with multiplicity two. The field of their contact divisor is \(K\). Since the degree-two collinearity divisor has already been completely accounted for, there are no further collinear fibres for this quotient.

111. Infinite rational family and nonconstant elliptic quotient

Put \(F_+=X^3Y+Y^3Z+Z^3X\), \(F_-=X^3Z+Y^3X+Z^3Y\), and

\[ C_\lambda:\ F_++\lambda F_-=0,\quad k=\frac{1+\lambda}{1-\lambda},\quad q=k^2. \]

The parameter \(\lambda\) is rational, with \(\lambda\ne\pm1\), and we restrict to smooth members. The invariant identities are

\[ F_++F_-=s_1^2s_2-s_1s_3-2s_2^2,\qquad F_+-F_-=-s_1 (X-Y)(Y-Z)(Z-X). \]

Consequently the quotient is the genus-one quartic

\[ \boxed{ E_\lambda:\quad W^2=1-(q+9)u+27u^2+(17q-27)u^3-27qu^4, } \]

with

\[ W=\frac{(q+27)v+2qu^2-(q+9)u+2}{2}. \]

Its binary-quartic invariants are \(I=3q(17q+18)\), \(J=27q(27q^2+44q+27)\), giving

\[ 4I^3-J^2=-27q^2(q+27)^2(31q^2+54q+27). \]

For rational \(q>0\) this is nonzero. The elliptic quotient has

\[ \boxed{j(E_\lambda)=-\frac{6912q(17q+18)^3}{(q+27)^2(31q^2+54q+27)}.} \]

The special fibres remain \(Q_\pm=(1/3,\pm k\sqrt{-3}/9)\), and

\[ C_\lambda\big|_{Z=-X-Y}=-(1+\lambda)(X^2+XY+Y^2)^2. \]

Thus their residual contact points remain \(P_\pm\) for every smooth rational member. The samples \(\lambda=0,2,3,-2,4\) were proved smooth over \(\mathbb Q\) by projective Jacobian-ideal calculations and all 25 sample finite-field substitution checks pass. Because smoothness is Zariski open and the \(j\)-map is nonconstant, infinitely many rational parameters give pairwise nonisomorphic elliptic quotients. A fixed genus-three curve has only finitely many automorphism subgroups of order three, so infinitely many nonisomorphic source curves also occur.

112. The two conjugate cubic W-models and exact descent

Over \(K=\mathbb Q(\omega)\), define

\[ T_+=\frac{s_1}{\ell_+},\qquad T_-=\frac{s_1}{\ell_-}. \]

Their respective pole divisors are \(f^*Q_+\) and \(f^*Q_-\); they are genuine nonrational-point W-models of degree three. The cyclic generator satisfies \(\sigma^*T_+=\omega T_+\), so \(T_+^3\) belongs to \(K(E_\lambda)\). Define

\[ A_+=1-\frac92u+\frac{27}{2}v-\frac{3\sqrt{-3}}2k(u-v-2u^2),\qquad A_-=\overline{A_+}. \]

The Fourier cubic identity gives \(T_\pm^3=A_\pm^{-1}\), and the discriminant identity gives \(A_+A_-=(1-3u)^3\). Therefore the two conjugate cubic extensions satisfy the exact norm relation

\[ \boxed{\operatorname{Norm}_{K/\mathbb Q}(T_+^3)=T_+^3T_-^3=(1-3u)^{-3}.} \]

This is an explicit model of the Galois descent condition from §107: the two cubic presentations are conjugate, their product lies in the cube classes of the rational function field, and the original quotient map and source curve descend over \(\mathbb Q\). It does not mean that a general pair of Kummer classes satisfying this norm relation always descends; the explicit curve supplies the remaining compatibility in this case. The rational degree-three global Jacobian projector is \(e=(1+\sigma_*+\sigma_*^2)/3=f^*f_*/3\), and \(e^2=e\).

113. A base-point-free bitangent eliminant

For the Klein quartic, search for lines \(Z=-AX-BY\), without choosing any rational point. If the restricted quartic has coefficients \(h_i\) in \(X^{4-i}Y^i\), necessary and sufficient square equations on \(h_0\ne0\) are

\[ 8h_0^2h_3-4h_0h_1h_2+h_1^3=0,\qquad 64h_0^3h_4-(4h_0h_2-h_1^2)^2=0. \]

An exact lexicographic Gröbner basis of these two equations has the second eliminant

\[ \boxed{B^{28}-3828B^{21}+87462B^{14}-83636B^7+1=0} \]

and a polynomial linear in \(A\). The rational-root theorem leaves \(B=\pm1\); only \(B=1\) is a root, giving \(A=1\). Lines with \(Z\)-coefficient zero are impossible because the restricted quartic has a nonzero \(XZ^3\) coefficient and zero \(Z^4\) coefficient, incompatible with a binary-quartic square. Thus \(X+Y+Z=0\) is the unique rational bitangent of \(C_0\). Its contact divisor is the irreducible degree-two polynomial \(X^2+XY+Y^2\). This is equation-only recovery of the two nonrational residual base points, without a rational-point search. On arbitrary coordinate-scrambled inputs exact lexicographic elimination may be expensive; no general fast algorithm is claimed.

114. Scope and next formal attacks

G02 now has a complete infinite family of explicit constructive test cases, with a cubic model over the quadratic field and verified descent. The general algorithmic G02 problem—solving the contact/elimination equations over arbitrary quadratic fields and descending the resulting maps—remains open. G03 is completed for this automorphism-recognizable family without supplying a rational point, but its arbitrary-curve form remains open. The Part XXIV P2 certificates are independently reverified, while general chart-I completeness and explicit chart-II cofactor certificates remain unresolved. The natural next attack is a rational-divisor or bitangent-guided incidence solver for arbitrary smooth quartics, including those with no rational point. The public monograph has not been deployed; this integration changes only local archive files.

Part XXVI. The exact solver over a quadratic field

115. Part XXV, checked

All 10 of Part XXV's tests pass in an isolated copy of the 1,542-file release. All 1,521 files of the Part XXIV tree are present byte for byte, and the only changed file is index.html.

Measured(indep_xxv.py, which imports nothing from quadratic_fibre_xxv/.) Write \(u=S_2/S_1^2\), \(v=S_3/S_1^3\), \(k=(1+\lambda)/(1-\lambda)\), \(q=k^2\) and \(W=\big((q+27)v+2qu^2-(q+9)u+2\big)/2\). Homogenize the quotient model (4) of §111 as \(W_h^2-\mathcal Q_h\), where \(\mathcal Q_h\) is the homogenized right-hand side of degree 8. This is divisible by \(F_\lambda\) for \(\lambda\in\{0,2,3,-2,4,\tfrac12,-\tfrac57\}\), and the quotient is a constant times the transposed quartic \(F'_\lambda\). The constants are \(28\), \(36\), \(\tfrac{31}4\), \(\tfrac{244}{81}\), \(\tfrac{268}{81}\), \(144\) and \(\tfrac{47677}{5184}\). The \(j\)-formula (6) agrees with an independent computation from the invariants of the binary quartic, \(j=6912I^3/(4I^3-J^2)\). At \(\lambda=0\) it gives \(-3375\), the classical CM-by-\(\sqrt{-7}\) quotient of the Klein quartic. At \(\lambda=2\) it gives \(-555579/7\).

CorrectionThe values \(\lambda\) and \(1/\lambda\) give the same \(j\), because \(C_{1/\lambda}\) is proportional to \(F'_\lambda\), the transpose of \(C_\lambda\). So the infinite family should be counted modulo \(\lambda\mapsto1/\lambda\). The conclusion of §111 is unchanged, since \(j\) is nonconstant.

DerivedThe geometry of §§109–112 fits the theorems of Parts XX and XXIV.

The map is the quotient by \(\sigma\), so every fibre is a \(\sigma\)-orbit. A collinear orbit of three distinct points spans a \(\sigma\)-invariant line, and the invariant lines are \(X+Y+Z=0\), \(\ell_+\) and \(\ell_-\). The first is a bitangent: \(F(X,Y,-X-Y)=-(X^2+XY+Y^2)^2\), and it touches \(C\) at both fixed points \(P_\pm\). So it carries no orbit. Each \(\ell_\pm\) passes through one fixed point and cuts out one orbit. These two orbits are exactly the two collinear fibres of Theorem 85.1, and they are conjugate.

The branch-sum law of Theorem 104.2 holds as follows. \(P_\pm\) lie on \(S_1=0\), so \(f(P_\pm)=\infty_\pm\). Also \(Q_++Q_-=\operatorname{div}(u-\tfrac13)+\infty_++\infty_-\), so \(2(Q_++Q_-)\sim2(\infty_++\infty_-)=B\).

The function \(T_+=S_1/\ell_+\) has \(\operatorname{div}T_+=P_++2P_--f^*Q_+\), and \(\sigma^*T_+=\omega T_+\). It is therefore the W-function of Theorem 104.1 at \(Q_+\), in Kummer form. The identity (7) is \((X+\omega Y+\omega^2Z)(X+\omega^2Y+\omega Z)=S_1^2-3S_2\).

The gradient at \(P_+\) is \((1+3\omega)(1,1,1)\). So the tangent at \(P_+\) is the bitangent, \(\ell_+\) is not tangent there, and \(P_+\) is a chart-I base point.

116. Chart-I discovery over \(\mathbb Q(\omega)\)

Part XXV built the quadratic example and its descent by hand. The test that G02 actually asks for is whether the general solver of §86 finds the map over the quadratic field when it is given only the curve and the conjugate point \(P_+=(1{:}\omega{:}\omega^2)\). That is the test run here.

Measured(qmod.sing, qmod_run.py, qverify_all.sing.) The method has three steps. First, the seven-equation system of §86 is built natively in Singular. Exact std over \(\mathbb Q(a)\), \(a^2+a+1=0\), did not finish in 10 minutes, so instead the system is solved over \(\mathbb F_p\) for six primes \(p\equiv1\pmod 3\), at both embeddings \(a\mapsto r\) of \(\omega\). Each run takes well under a second and gives a single reduced solution (vdim 1) in every one of the 24 runs. Second, each coordinate \(x_0+x_1\omega\) is recovered from the two embeddings by CRT and rational reconstruction. Third, the reconstructed point is verified exactly over \(\mathbb Q(\omega)\), with no modular step.

Table 23. The chart-I pencil at \(P_+=(1{:}\omega{:}\omega^2)\) on \(C_\lambda\), found by the solver and verified exactly over \(\mathbb Q(\omega)\).
\(\lambda\)\((s,\ b_0,\ c_0)\)\(\ell\)\(N_0\)\(j\)(target)\(G(1,t)\)
0 (Klein)\(\big(\tfrac{5+4\omega}{21},\ -\tfrac{1+2\omega}3,\ \tfrac{3+\omega}{21}\big)\)\(\propto\ell_+\)\(\propto\ell_-\)\(-3375\)\(c\,t^2\cdot\)irreducible sextic
2\(\big(-\tfrac{1+2\omega}9,\ -\tfrac{1+2\omega}3,\ -\tfrac{1+\omega}9\big)\)\(\propto\ell_+\)\(\propto\ell_-\)\(-555579/7\)\(c\,t^2\cdot\)irreducible sextic

For both curves all seven equations vanish identically over \(\mathbb Q(\omega)\). The residual \(\kappa\) is \(t\)-free and of degree 3 in \(z\). The sextic factor of \(G(1,t)\) is irreducible over \(\mathbb Q(\omega)\), so by Theorem 86.1 the map has degree exactly 3. The target's \(j\)-invariant is rational and equal to \(j(E_\lambda)\).

The outputs match the predictions of Part XXIV exactly. The pencil's line is \(\ell_+\), which carries the collinear fibre over \(Q_+\). Its reducible member is \(H\cdot\ell_-\), so by Theorem 105.3 the second base point is the residual point on \(N_0=\ell_-\), namely \(P_-=\bar P_+\). One solve over \(\mathbb Q(\omega)\) therefore delivers both conjugate base points, the elliptic target with its rational \(j\), and the degree-3 map. That is the descent of §112 recovered by the general method rather than written down.

ScopeThe solution count (one) is a modular count: 24 runs, all with vdim 1. It is not a certificate. The Klein quartic has many elliptic quotients, from its 28 subgroups of order 3, but the system at \(P_+\) has exactly one solution modulo every prime tested. A completeness certificate in the sense of §95 over \(\mathbb Q(\omega)\) is the next mechanical step. The base point itself was supplied. Part XXV's bitangent eliminant, which finds \(X+Y+Z=0\) and hence \(P_\pm\) without a point, and this solver, which goes from \(P_+\) to the map, together form a complete point-free pipeline for this class. The pipeline uses the class's symmetry only through the bitangent's contact points.

117. Status after Part XXVI

For the cyclic family \(C_\lambda\), G02 is now settled in the form the audit asked for. There is an explicit smooth quartic with quadratic-conjugate collinear fibres (Part XXV). A solver over that quadratic field recovers the map from the conjugate point alone (§116). The descent to \(\mathbb Q\) is visible in the output, because \(N_0=\bar\ell\) and \(j\in\mathbb Q\). What remains open has three parts. First, certified completeness over \(\mathbb Q(\omega)\). Second, examples whose quadratic base points do not come from an automorphism, which is the descent problem of §107 without symmetry. Third, G03 for curves whose base points are neither rational nor contact points of a rational bitangent. The public page has not been republished.

Reproducibility. Part XXVI adds quadratic_solver_xxvi/. It contains indep_xxv.py and its receipt (independent quotient-identity and \(j\) checks), bitangent_check.txt, qmod.sing (the §86 system over any base field, with the base point given as a matrix), qmod_run.py (modular solve at both embeddings, then CRT and rational reconstruction in \(\mathbb Q(\omega)\)), qmod_lam0.json, qmod_lam2.json, and qverify_all.sing with its output qverify_all.out (exact verification over \(\mathbb Q(a)\)). The Part XXV monograph is kept as index_before_part_xxvi.html.

The construction in §121 specifies a map. The discovery input in this section consists solely of the fifteen rational coefficients in asymmetric_quartic.json. The parameter family in §124 admits the same line search in the displayed rational coordinates. Its fibre lines u±qv=0u\pm qv=0 have height one independently of the parameter. The residual point supplies a linear factor on each line, and the uniform square identity is verified symbolically. A separate equation-only run at m=1112m=1112 also reconstructs the rational target.

Proposition 122.1 (positive search). Suppose a smooth rational plane quartic has a degree-three elliptic map with two conjugate collinear fibre lines L,L‾L,\bar L in a quadratic field, a residual point PP defined over that field, and a nondegenerate §86 chart-I pencil with frame (L,HP,L‾)(L,H_P,\bar L) and g6≠0g_6\ne0. A point-free search is guaranteed to return a certified chart-I pencil. To remove the fixed bounds, normalize each line at its first nonzero coefficient, write each other coefficient as (a+bd)/c(a+b\sqrt d)/c in primitive integers with c>0c>0, and enumerate shells by the maximum of |d|,|a|,|b|,c|d|,|a|,|b|,c. Each shell is finite and the witnessing line lies in one of them. Factorization on that line reaches PP, or its conjugate. Rescaling frame axes only rescales z,tz,t and the leading coefficient, so the corresponding square test succeeds. This is the implemented --dovetail mode. It gives a positive termination theorem under the stated incidence hypotheses. Negative termination, a uniform height bound in arbitrary coordinates, and general descent of other accepted pencils remain open.

123. Trivial automorphism group and uniqueness of the elliptic quotient

Let T0∈Sym4V*T_0\in\operatorname{Sym}^4 V^* be the symmetric tensor of the primitive rational equation of C⊂ℙ(V)C\subset\mathbb P(V), V=ℚ3V=\mathbb Q^3. Uniqueness of the degree-three elliptic quotient

Let D=(kerf*)0⊂J(C)D=(\ker f_*)^0\subset J(C). The identity f*f*=[3]f_* f^*=[3] gives an isogeny J(C)∼E×DJ(C)\sim E\times D over ℚ\mathbb Q. The smooth model at 11 gives good reduction of J(C)J(C), hence of DD (for example by the unramified Tate-module criterion). Direct enumeration of the three disjoint projective charts gives #C(𝔽11)=18\#C(\mathbb F_{11})=18, #C(𝔽121)=164\#C(\mathbb F_{121})=164. The elliptic curve has trace zero at 11. Subtracting its contribution from the first two power sums gives −6,−20-6,-20 for the surface. Reciprocity then gives its characteristic polynomial P(U)=U4+6U3+28U2+66U+121. P(U)=U^4+6U^3+28U^2+66U+121 . It is irreducible over ℚ\mathbb Q, and the quotient-of-roots resultant factors there as ResU(P(U),P(vU))=14641(v−1)4(11v4−6v3+2v2−6v+11)2(121v4+220v3+234v2+220v+121). \operatorname{Res}_U(P(U),P(vU)) =14641(v-1)^4 (11v^4-6v^3+2v^2-6v+11)^2 (121v^4+220v^3+234v^2+220v+121). Both quartic factors are primitive, irreducible and nonmonic. Neither contains a root of unity. For every n>0n>0 the four nn-th powers of the Frobenius eigenvalues are therefore distinct. They form a single Galois orbit as PP is irreducible. Every positive power of Frobenius has irreducible characteristic polynomial over ℚ\mathbb Q. An elliptic subvariety of the special fibre over 𝔽¯11\overline{\mathbb F}_{11} would be defined over some finite extension, and its degree-two Frobenius polynomial would divide this degree-four irreducible polynomial. Thus DD has geometrically simple reduction. Geometric nonsimplicity in characteristic zero would supply a nontrivial rational idempotent in the endomorphism algebra after finite extension, surviving under injective specialization for good reduction. This contradicts simplicity. In particular DD has no elliptic quotient over ℚ¯\overline{\mathbb Q}.

Every morphism g:Cℚ¯→E′g:C_{\overline{\mathbb Q}}\to E' to an elliptic curve, after translation, is induced by a homomorphism of J(C)J(C), hence kills DD. Both ff and gg factor through the Abel–Jacobi map followed by J(C)→J(C)/DJ(C)\to J(C)/D. The last quotient is an elliptic curve. Its map to EE is an isogeny. If that isogeny had degree bigger than one then, since degf=3\deg f=3, the map from CC to J(C)/DJ(C)/D would have degree one, impossible for genus three. Hence the quotient is isomorphic to EE. Applying the same degree count to any gg of degree three gives uniqueness up to target isomorphism and translation. The only residual points for any such map are therefore P±P_\pm, and both are in chart I. This geometric classification makes no assertion about the scheme multiplicities of the shape equations.

124. Pairwise nonisomorphic covers of one elliptic curve

Keep q2=2q^2=2 and set b=m+qb=m+q, c=m−qc=m-q for m=1+1111km=1+1111k, kk a nonnegative integer. Use the same expressions for A,B,FA,B,F and for x,yx,y. Since 1111=11⋅1011111=11\cdot101, the special fibres at both primes coincide term for term with their counterparts at m=1m=1. Every isomorphism between two sources must consequently give an automorphism of EE carrying the unordered pair of collinearity points {Q+,Q−}\{Q_+,Q_-\} to itself and one branch divisor to the other. Write this automorphism as translation by RR after an origin-preserving automorphism. On y2=x3+2y^2=x^3+2 every origin-preserving automorphism has the form (x,y)↦(ζx,±y)(x,y)\mapsto(\zeta x,\pm y) with ζ3=1\zeta^3=1, as follows directly by comparing coefficients in a Weierstrass change of variables. It preserves the specified pair. Consequently the translation alone preserves it. Summing the points gives 2R=02R=0. Their difference has order three since the tangent y=qy=q meets the cubic three times at Q+Q_+, so RR also lies in the group generated by Q+Q_+. Hence R=0R=0.

The functions HmH_m have common pole divisor 4O4O. Equality of two branch divisors after the indicated origin-preserving change forces Hm(x,y)H_m(x,y) and Hn(ζx,±y)H_n(\zeta x,\pm y) to be proportional. The functions 1,x,y,x21,x,y,x^2 are independent by their distinct pole orders. Comparing the ratio of the xx and x2x^2 coefficients gives 18m2−2=ζ−118n2−2. \frac{18}{m^2-2}=\zeta^{-1}\frac{18}{n^2-2}. Both sides without the root of unity are nonzero rationals. Thus ζ=1\zeta=1, and positivity of the parameters gives m=nm=n. In particular the whole sequence consists of geometrically pairwise nonisomorphic plane quartics, all mapping to the same rational elliptic curve.

Scope of the classification. The characteristic-zero ideal calculation settles the complete normalized chart-I schemes at the two quadratic points of each of the two cyclic test curves. In the asymmetric sequence the conclusion is geometric and global: every degree-three elliptic map is the displayed map up to target isomorphism and translation, and its two collinear fibres are precisely the conjugate pair. A general chart-scheme multiplicity theorem for those asymmetric curves would require a further argument. For arbitrary plane quartics, a point-free algorithm able to decide nonexistence or to certify exhaustion of all base-point fields is still open.

The code and recorded outputs for §§118–124 are in quadratic_completeness_xxvii/. Running python -B verify_release.py there rebuilds the numerical and algebraic receipts with SymPy. The proof of geometric simplicity in §123 can also be expressed using Howe and Zhu’s finite-field criterion for powers of Frobenius. Howe and Zhu, Journal of Number Theory 92 (2002), 139–163, Proposition 3.

Part XXVIII. Exhausting the degree-three elliptic quotients of a plane quartic

125. A finite decision procedure from the quartic equation

Let CC be a smooth plane quartic over ℚ\mathbb Q. A geometric class is a degree-three morphism Cℚ¯→EC_{\overline{\mathbb Q}}\to E to a smooth genus-one target, modulo isomorphisms of the target, including translations. Equivalently it is a genus-one subfield of index three in ℚ¯(C)\overline{\mathbb Q}(C). This convention keeps the source coordinates fixed. A class defined over ℚ\mathbb Q gives a rational genus-one quotient. A rational origin on its target is a further arithmetic condition.

Theorem 125.1. Twelve explicitly given ideals over ℚ\mathbb Q have finite geometric support. From the equation of CC alone, their combined support yields precisely its geometric classes, with exact cubic map coordinates and a test for duplicate classes. Gröbner elimination and factorization terminate in exact arithmetic. Sections 126–127 give two independent checks on the result: the fixed divisor of each cubic net has length three, and there are at most 840 geometric classes on any one source. The unit ideal on every chart is a certificate of nonexistence. Good reduction and symmetry can certify exhaustion without computing the twelve full bases.

The positive search of §122 is useful when a short coefficient search finds a map. The theorem here includes curves with no elliptic factor, points of arbitrary field within the bound of §127, and pencils at which the marked line is tangent.

Indeed, RR records the ratios of pairs of roots. For every n>0n>0 the partition of the roots given by equality of their NnNn-th powers is already the partition given by their NN-th powers. The degrees of their conjugacy orbits therefore stay fixed under all further powers. If an elliptic factor exists geometrically, it is defined over some finite extension. For an ordinary elliptic factor the two eigenvalues, over a common extension of degree divisible by NN, have slopes 0,10,1. They are distinct, have a conjugacy orbit of size two, and are exchanged by complex conjugation. Already at NN they yield a quadratic factor with constant term pNp^N and trace prime to pp. For a supersingular elliptic factor the ratio of the two eigenvalues is a root of unity. Its two eigenvalues, along with their conjugates after a further extension, collapse at NN to a rational number ±pN/2\pm p^{N/2}. Conversely an ordinary quadratic of the indicated form is the Frobenius polynomial of an elliptic curve by the finite-field classification. A rational Weil number ±pN/2\pm p^{N/2} likewise represents a supersingular elliptic isogeny class over 𝔽pN\mathbb F_{p^N}. The isogeny classification identifies either class as a factor. This argument uses Waterhouse’s Theorem 4.1 and the Tate–Honda correspondence. Waterhouse, Abelian varieties over finite fields (1969)

If this residue-field test excludes a geometric elliptic factor, no nonconstant map from Cℚ¯C_{\overline{\mathbb Q}} to any elliptic curve exists. Such a map gives an elliptic quotient of the Jacobian over a finite extension. Good reduction of the Jacobian persists there. Complete reducibility gives a rational idempotent projector onto that elliptic factor, which extends after clearing its denominator to the abelian scheme over the local ring. On a prime-to-pp Tate module the specialization of the projector has the same rank two. It therefore defines an elliptic factor of the special fibre, a contradiction. A residue-field elliptic factor leaves the characteristic-zero existence question open.

Now fix a positive integer MM and any integral equation F+F_+ of a smooth plane quartic, including one with a degree-three elliptic quotient. Choose a witnessing r∤Mr\nmid M. If it terminates affirmatively on a positive input, the finite transcript uses a single common modulus MM. The construction gives a negative input with the same transcript. This isolates the information supplied by the exact characteristic-zero incidence calculations elsewhere in this part.

133. Exhaustion, arithmetic descent, and reproducibility

The geometric problem has a terminating equation-only solution for every smooth plane quartic over ℚ\mathbb Q. The unrestricted algorithm solves twelve ideals in characteristic zero, reconstructs the cubic nets, and groups their differential directions. The bound of 840 is an upper bound; the paper makes no claim that it is attained. It limits the field degree of a single geometric class to 840 and of a marked class to 1680. The splitting field of J[3]J[3] contains the fields of the unmarked classes. Good reduction can exclude every elliptic factor. When the elliptic part of a good reduction has dimension one, verifying a single degree-three map proves exhaustion.

Smooth source over ℚ\mathbb Q Complete geometric result Certificate used
Fermat and rational split-diagonal twists 16 classes of degree three; each cyclic Polarized Gaussian lattice, explicit cyclic maps and Hessian recognition
C0,1,3C_{0,1,3} and the §129 congruence class No degree three; exact spectrum 2ℤ>02\mathbb Z_{>0} Three geometrically nonisogenous sign quotients at 11
Klein perturbation DD of §130 No elliptic map of any degree Independent geometric exclusions at 7 and 11

The last row also illustrates a general positive certificate. Sum the degrees with multiplicity of the elliptic Frobenius factors after the power in §130, and divide by two. If the resulting geometric elliptic part has dimension one, specialization bounds the characteristic-zero elliptic part by one. A verified degree-three map then identifies its unique elliptic subvariety and, by optimality, the unique class. The computation uses just the input equation; it does not require its parameter label.

The distinction between theorem and benchmark matters for computation. All four rows were classified by executed exact routes. The full moving-point tangent locus on the Fermat curve was also eliminated, and full fixed-point tangent ideals with positive and empty support were solved and replayed by polynomial certificates. All twelve unrestricted chart generators were tested. The release supplies the unrestricted solver and proof-producing mode; no full twelve-chart Gröbner run on a generic large-coefficient quartic is claimed. There is no established practical time bound for that route.

For rational arithmetic, a fixed class descends as a genus-one quotient. A quartic of index one makes its stable targets pointed. Section 132 constructs a rational target for any certified stable quadratic chart and gives the explicit degree-twelve Fermat map even when a degree-three pointed target is impossible. A general unconditional algorithm deciding rational points on every resulting genus-one torsor is outside these results.

The verification program, source equations, chart certificates, reconstructed maps and exact outputs are in exhaustion_xxviii/. The integrated monograph retains the previous edition under index_before_part_xxviii.html.

Derived(The bound of §127.) The isotropy of \(B[3]\) can be confirmed directly. If \(\Theta|_B=M^{\otimes3}\) with \(M\) principal, the Weil pairing of \(J[3]\) restricts to \(B[3]\) as \(e^{M^9}\), that is, \(e_9(x,\lambda_My)\). This is trivial on \(B[3]\), because there \(e_9(3x',y)=e_9(x',3y)=1\). The pairing that is nondegenerate on \(B[3]\) is \(B\)'s own \(e^{M^3}\), not \(J\)'s. The counts \(\prod_{i=1}^3(3^i+1)=1120\) and \((3^6-1)(3^5-3)/((3^2-1)(3^2-3))=3640\) are correct, so the bound \(\tfrac14\cdot1120\cdot3=840\) stands.

Measured(fermat_sylow.py, which does not use fermat_lattice.py.) \(\operatorname{Aut}(X^4+Y^4+Z^4)\) has order 96, with 32 elements of order 3 forming 16 subgroups. Each subgroup has exactly two fixed points on the curve, so by Riemann–Hurwitz each quotient has genus 1. This independently gives the 16 cyclic classes of §128 as a lower bound. The lattice computation is what excludes any others. The statement that the descended targets have no real point has a one-line proof. The Fermat quartic has no real point, and the fibre of a degree-3 map over a real point is a real divisor of odd degree, which must contain a real point.

Measured(lpoly2.py, cyclo_check.py.) The point counts \((8,50,281)\) at 7 and \((12,120,1335)\) at 11 were recomputed for \(X^3Y+Y^3Z+Z^3X+30X^4\) with the galois package, and checked against brute force over \(\mathbb F_p\). They reproduce exactly, and so do the Frobenius polynomials. At 7 the cyclotomic orders of the root ratios are \(\{1,3\}\), and \(P_6=(U^2+245U+7^6)^3\) with \(v_7(245)=2\). The slopes are therefore \(1/3,2/3\), which no elliptic curve has. A first reading of \(P_3=(T^2-21T+343)^3\) as "a cube of an elliptic curve" is wrong for the same reason. At 11 no nontrivial ratio is a root of unity, and \(P_2\) is an irreducible sextic. Both exclusions of §130 hold independently.

135. The twelve-chart atlas, timed

Negative result(run_atlas.py.) The chart ideals emitted by free_atlas.py emit were run in Singular 4.3 on two inputs: \(C^\star\) modulo 32003, and the Klein\(+30X^4\) control modulo 7. The first four charts of \(C^\star\) each ran past a 120 s cap. The representative chart 012_I then ran past 1,600 s on both inputs, at about 1.5–1.65 GB, without finishing. This was modulo a prime, with no coefficient growth. Each chart carries the base point as unknowns \((u,v,d)\) together with the curve equation. That is the formulation whose mod-\(p\) Gröbner basis already failed to finish in §87 (freeP.lib). Theorem 125.1 is a valid terminating procedure, but at present it is not a practical one: its termination guarantee says nothing about runtime, and on these inputs it does not finish in half an hour per chart even in characteristic \(p\).

136. Point-free discovery by residue-field scanning

The fixed-point system of §86 solves in a fraction of a second modulo \(p\). That suggests the opposite strategy to the atlas: enumerate the base point instead of eliminating it. There are only about \(p\) points to try.

Algorithm 136.1For a prime \(p\) of good reduction, solve the fixed-point chart-I system modulo \(p\) at every \(P\in C(\mathbb F_p)\), and record the set \(H_p\) of points carrying a pencil. If no coordinate rotation gives a nondegenerate frame at some \(P\), it is re-tested after a random projective change of coordinates. No point is left untested. Next, choose hits consistently across primes and reconstruct them by CRT and rational reconstruction. Keep the points that lie on \(C\) exactly, and run the exact solver of §86 at each. For base points over a quadratic field \(K\), use primes that split in \(K\) and reconstruct each coordinate \(x_0+x_1\theta\) from the two embeddings.

A class whose marked collinear fibre has a rational base point \(P\) produces a hit at \(P\bmod p\) at every good prime, apart from the finitely many where \(g_6\) or the frame degenerates. A hit is only a candidate: it may come from a map that exists only in characteristic \(p\). The exact solve over \(\mathbb Q\) or \(K\) is the filter, and every reported map is verified there.

On \(C^\star\) and the family curve, the scan finds both base points without any search over \(C(\mathbb Q)\) or any supplied point. These are the same points that Part XX found by height search and Theorem 105.3 found from one of them. On \(C_2\), the inert primes give no hits and the split primes give the conjugate pair, exactly as the quadratic field of definition predicts. The whole run costs about \(\#C(\mathbb F_p)\times0.2\) s per prime.

ScopeThe scan covers chart I at \(\mathbb F_p\)-rational base points. A class whose base points generate a larger field needs scans over \(\mathbb F_{p^k}\). Chart II needs its own fixed-point solver in the scan. An empty scan is evidence, not a certificate: the certificates of nonexistence remain those of §95 and §130. Within those limits, Algorithm 136.1 is the first base-point-free method in this program that finishes in practice, measured here in minutes. The atlas of §125 did not finish one chart in half an hour.

137. Status after Part XXIX

Part XXVIII's exhaustion theory checks out, and so do its three worked classifications and its two-prime obstruction. Its general atlas, though, is not yet usable on an ordinary input. Residue-field scanning closes much of the practical gap for G03. From the equation alone it recovers rational and split-quadratic base points, which the exact solvers of Parts XX and XXVI turn into verified maps. Three items remain open: a chart-II scan, scans over \(\mathbb F_{p^k}\) for base points in larger fields, and combining scanning with a certified completeness bound, for instance by comparing the hit count with the 840-class bound or with the number of elliptic factors detected at \(p\). The public page has not been republished.

Reproducibility. Part XXIX adds pointfree_xxix/. It contains the independent checks lpoly2.py, cyclo_check.py and fermat_sylow.py with their receipts, and the atlas timing runner run_atlas.py with its logs. It also contains the scanner scan_points.py (with qmod_safe.sing, the §86 system with a degenerate-frame guard) and the pipelines discover_pointfree.py and discover_quadratic.py with their receipts. The Part XXVIII monograph is kept as index_before_part_xxix.html.

Part XXX. Certifying residue-field discovery of elliptic quotients

138. From modular marks to a complete answer

Let C:F(X,Y,Z)=0C:F(X,Y,Z)=0 be a smooth plane quartic over ℚ\mathbb Q. A cubic quotient class is a genus-one subfield of index three in ℚ¯(C)\overline{\mathbb Q}(C). Target coordinates and translations give the same class. A mark specifies one of the collinear fibres of §85, or equivalently its fibre line and residual point on CC. The two marks are counted with multiplicity. A rational class means the embedded subfield descends to ℚ\mathbb Q. Its smooth genus-one target may have index two.

Theorem 138.1. At any chosen prime p>3p>3 of smooth plane reduction, one can determine a single finite residue field in which every geometric special class has a mark. A deterministic scan over that field finds all special classes and gives a certified upper bound on the characteristic-zero count. Successive congruences at the same prime, interleaved with exact positive recovery, give a terminating decision procedure for the generic count, including when some special classes have no lift. It uses fixed-point, fixed-line calculations and linear lifting. The required residue field can still be very large. The theorem gives no uniform bound on the required pp-adic precision.

The numerical distinction is already visible over 𝔽13\mathbb F_{13}. A smooth quartic can have a degree-three mark at every rational point and have zero geometric cubic quotients in characteristic zero. Conversely, the twist 2X4+Y4+Z4=02X^4+Y^4+Z^4=0 has no marks over 𝔽25\mathbb F_{25} and has sixteen geometric quotients, all visible over 𝔽625\mathbb F_{625}. Sections 139–143 give the certificates and the termination proof. The last sections determine complete degree spectra and the fields of the marked points in further families.

Audit of §§134–137. Direct comparison of the two ZIP payloads preserved every one of the 1,624 Part XXVIII files, accounting for the previous index under its new name. All thirteen Part XXVIII verification groups ran again. The stored §135 measurements are right-censored observations for two modular chart-I jobs, one on C⋆C^\star at 32003 and one on the negative control at 7. Each exceeded 1,600 seconds. The smaller four-chart trial used 120 seconds. There is no characteristic-zero runtime measurement in those logs. The new computations use independent finite arithmetic and the full pair of charts.

Three implementation details matter for reproducing the handoff. The two public discovery scripts in Part XXIX call the basic scanner; the random-frame retry is a separate entry point. Each archived positive scan reports zero untested points. The original chart test asks for the geometric support dimension after fixing an 𝔽p\mathbb F_p point: its returned conic parameters can live over an extension. The split-quadratic script itself checks the reconstructed point on the quartic; the map certificate is supplied in §116. Finally, the §134 power-polynomial cross-check rounded numerical roots. We recomputed the powered polynomials by exact resultants and confirmed the exclusions at 7 and 11. The solver below enumerates every field-rational mark in both charts, including its normalized conic data.

The normalized-coordinate CRT search in §136 also requires the coordinate support to agree at every prime. Projective support can change under reduction, for example at 2, 3 and 5 for (2:3:5)(2:3:5). Section 143 supplies a bounded-height reconstruction using the full projective congruences.

139. A finite residue field that sees every geometric class

Let the rational smooth plane quartic have smooth reduction CpC_p at p>3p>3, and let JpJ_p be its principally polarized Jacobian. A class is a degree-three map to a smooth genus-one curve up to target isomorphism. A mark is one of its collinear fibres, with double marks counted once when describing the support. Use π\pi for arithmetic Frobenius acting on the geometric points of JpJ_p and P(T)=det(T−π∣VℓJp)P(T)=\det(T-\pi\mid V_\ell J_p) for its Weil characteristic polynomial, at any ℓ≠p\ell\ne p.

Specialization and separation. Specialization injects the geometric characteristic-zero classes into the geometric characteristic-pp classes and respects the decomposition group action. The correspondence of §127 uses the elliptic subvariety B⊂JB\subset J of restricted polarization degree three. Extend scalars so the subvariety and the relevant three-torsion points are defined. Choose a Lagrangian H⊃B[3]H\supset B[3]. The principally polarized quotient J/HJ/H has good reduction, since HH extends as a finite étale subgroup. Its principal elliptic factor πH(B)\pi_H(B) and its complement have good reduction by the prime-to-pp Tate module criterion. Their product decomposition and its inverse extend over the valuation ring by the extension property of abelian schemes. The reverse correspondence in the special fibre gives a degree-three elliptic subvariety there with the specialized three-torsion plane. Indeed that plane maps to zero under πH\pi_H, and the identity component of the preimage of the extended principal factor is an abelian scheme: πH\pi_H is finite étale and the component group of its preimage is finite étale. In particular the same nine sections lie in the identity component. Equivalently extend the elliptic inclusion itself and its polarized dual. Their composite on the elliptic scheme is [3][3], so the kernel in every fibre lies in the étale three-torsion. Its special fibre is trivial, since the original map on the finite étale three-torsion is injective. This extends BB as an elliptic subvariety with the same restricted polarization. Distinct generic three-torsion planes stay distinct by good reduction. The argument works over a finite extension and commutes with conjugation. Every special cubic class is separable because p>3p>3.

An intersection estimate also gives a simple way to group answers in the special fibre. For distinct elliptic subvarieties B1,B2B_1,B_2 of restricted degree three put S=B1+B2S=B_1+B_2 and m=length(B1∩B2)m=\operatorname{length}(B_1\cap B_2). Addition a:B1×B2→Sa:B_1\times B_2\to S is an isogeny of degree mm. Its pulled-back polarization D=a*ΘD=a^*\Theta has intersection three with each coordinate fibre. If D0D_0 is three times the sum of the coordinate fibres, then (D−D0)⋅D0=0(D-D_0)\cdot D_0=0. The surface Hodge index inequality gives D2≤D02=18D^2\le D_0^2=18. Thus mχ(Θ|S)≤9m\chi(\Theta|_S)\le9. A principal restriction on SS would split the indecomposable Jacobian, so χ(Θ|S)≥2\chi(\Theta|_S)\ge2 and m≤4m\le4, including nonreduced intersection. In particular B↦B[3]B\mapsto B[3] stays injective, since a shared plane would have length nine. The dual of B1×B2→SB_1\times B_2\to S has prime-to-pp degree. The map Jp→B1∨×B2∨J_p\to B_1^\vee\times B_2^\vee factors through the smooth abelian quotient Jp→S∨J_p\to S^\vee followed by this separable isogeny. Its pullback on differentials has rank two. Consequently distinct classes have distinct projective canonical differential lines, an exact duplicate test in characteristic p>3p>3.

A single field suffices. Let ee be the least n>0n>0 such that TnT^n is a nonzero constant in 𝔽3[T]/(Pmod3)\mathbb F_3[T]/(P\bmod3). By Cayley–Hamilton πe\pi^e acts on Jp[3]J_p[3] by a scalar. All special three-torsion planes are then stable under πe\pi^e. The injectivity just proved makes each corresponding class defined over 𝔽pe\mathbb F_{p^e}. The determinant of evaluation in §85 produces a nonzero rational divisor of marks of degree two on each target, so all marks are defined over 𝔽p2e\mathbb F_{p^{2e}}. That argument is valid in characteristic p>3p>3: the cover is separable, the residual point of a moving collinear fibre would define a morphism from genus one to genus three, and such a nonconstant morphism remains impossible in positive characteristic after separating off a Frobenius power. Each mark gives a rational fibre line, residual point and normalized chart parameters over that same field. The two chart equations in §125 use denominators of characteristic at most three (the Taylor coefficients can equivalently be obtained by polynomial substitution); the converse pole and field-degree arguments also hold here. Enumerating both chart types at every point, in all necessary frames, and all parameters over this finite field therefore finds every special geometric class. Their number bounds the generic geometric count above. Matching that count with distinct exact characteristic-zero maps certifies exhaustion. In particular an empty complete special scan proves nonexistence in characteristic zero.

For counts restricted to classes defined over ℚ\mathbb Q, each generic class specializes to a Frobenius-fixed special class. Its two marks are already visible over 𝔽p2\mathbb F_{p^2}. Enumerate the special classes represented in that quadratic extension and retain those invariant under pp-power Frobenius, equivalently those with projective differential line defined over 𝔽p\mathbb F_p. This bounds the rational count above. A fixed special class can fail to lift. A map defined over ℚ\mathbb Q as a genus-one quotient can also have a target without a rational origin, as in §132.

To obtain a dimension-only bound, use the reciprocal coefficient list 1,a,b,c,μb,μ2a,μ3,μ=pmod3. 1,a,b,c,\mu b,\mu^2 a,\mu^3,\qquad \mu=p\bmod3. In each multiplier there are 27 triples modulo three. In the order μ=1,2\mu=1,2 the largest scalar exponents in the two lists are 36 and 40. One proves the finite enumeration by starting with 11 in the six-dimensional algebra, multiplying by TT and reducing with the monic polynomial until the five nonconstant coefficients vanish. The executable proof loops over all 54 triples, including those for which the polynomial has repeated roots. For example the extremal coefficient lists in the receipt attain their indicated exponents as polynomial-quotient calculations. A single residue extension of degree at most 72 if p≡1(mod3)p\equiv1\pmod3 and 80 if p≡2(mod3)p\equiv2\pmod3 suffices. The choice is the computed degree 2e2e; a universal choice of exactly 72 or 80 need not contain every required subfield. This is an existence bound on the exhaustive finite computation; its largest fields are far too large for naive enumeration.

Shrinking the scan field. Let NN be the least common multiple of the orders of all roots of unity among ratios of the complex roots of PP. The resultant ResT(P(T),P(VT))\operatorname{Res}_T(P(T),P(VT)) computes these orders by cyclotomic factorization. Semisimplicity of Frobenius implies that the centralizer of πNs\pi^{Ns} on VℓJpV_\ell J_p equals that of πN\pi^N for every positive ss, since both powers partition the eigenvalues identically. Every geometric endomorphism is defined over a finite extension, so commutes with some πNs\pi^{Ns}; it therefore commutes with πN\pi^N and is defined over 𝔽pN\mathbb F_{p^N}. Apply this to the polarized norm endomorphism with image BB. Every class field degree divides gcd(e,N)\gcd(e,N). The semisimplicity fact and faithful Tate-module realization are standard. Tate, Endomorphisms of abelian varieties over finite fields, Theorem 2 (1966).

For a tighter bound, form the powered polynomial at n=lcm(2,N)n=\operatorname{lcm}(2,N) as in §130. Each rational linear factor and each ordinary elliptic quadratic factor determines a geometric elliptic isotypic component. Recover its polynomial PiP_i over 𝔽p\mathbb F_p by collecting precisely the irreducible factors of PP, with multiplicities, whose nnth powers give that factor. This component is defined over 𝔽p\mathbb F_p. Indeed its central idempotent is a rational polynomial in πn\pi^n, and the image after clearing denominators gives the actual abelian subvariety. Two distinguishable factors at nn cannot merge later by the definition of NN. Every geometric elliptic subvariety lies in one such component. Set Di=1D_i=1 for a component of dimension one. Otherwise compute Di=gcd(e(Pi),N(Pi))D_i=\gcd(e(P_i),N(P_i)) as above on that abelian subvariety. One may scan the individual degrees 2Di2D_i, or a single extension of degree 2lcmiDi2\operatorname{lcm}_i D_i. With no such components the Weil polynomial alone excludes every elliptic quotient. The accompanying checker recomputes the Weil polynomials of the displayed sources by two point counters before deriving these field bounds.

Comparing and counting the unmarked maps

Let the degree-six polar functions of two accepted marked pencils be zi=Ai/Biz_i=A_i/B_i with ternary conics Ai,BiA_i,B_i. The unmarked subfields agree precisely when the nine degree-eight forms A1iB12−iA2jB22−j,0≤i,j≤2 A_1^iB_1^{2-i}A_2^jB_2^{2-j},\qquad 0\le i,j\le2 are linearly dependent modulo FF. For equal subfields, the two degree-two functions on their common target map it to a curve of bidegree at most (2,2)(2,2) in ℙ1×ℙ1\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1. Conversely a nontrivial relation in this range implies the compositum k(z1,z2)k(z_1,z_2) has degree at most two over either k(zi)k(z_i). The two degrees are equal since both functions have degree six on the same source. If the common degree is one, the rational fields agree. If it is two, this compositum is already the unique quadratic subfield above each rational field inside the source. Two different quadratic subfields in a degree-six extension in odd characteristic would generate a subfield of degree four. In either case the two degree-three quotient subfields coincide. This comparison works in positive characteristic without an assumption about distinguishable tangent directions. The scanner applies the same test to coefficientwise Frobenius, obtaining a permutation of actual subfields.

At good reduction in characteristic p>3p>3, a complete both-chart scan over 𝔽p2\mathbb F_{p^2} captures every 𝔽p\mathbb F_p-defined degree-three quotient. Indeed the determinant divisor of §85 on its genus-one target has degree two and is Frobenius-stable. Its construction works verbatim here: finite flatness, Riemann–Roch and separability give the determinant degree; Riemann–Hurwitz excludes a nonconstant map from the target back to the plane quartic in this argument (also factor out any purely inseparable Frobenius). Its support splits in the quadratic extension; the residual point and fibre line are defined over the same field as the mark. Counting the Frobenius-fixed classes in the exhaustive quadratic scan is consequently exact. A reduction with extra special-fibre maps can increase this number. Conversely, for good reduction, specialization carries a characteristic-zero rational class to a residue-field fixed class. The specialized elliptic subvariety has polarization degree three; different source classes have distinct 3-torsion planes by §127, and prime-to-pp torsion specializes isomorphically. The finite-field count is therefore an upper bound on rational characteristic-zero quotient classes. Exact characteristic-zero witnesses attaining it give exhaustion. An empty quadratic scan proves the absence of rational classes even with no other local decomposition of the Jacobian. This statement bounds genus-one quotient classes; a rational origin on the descended target is the index question of §132.

141. A terminating single-prime decision procedure

Why repeated local pruning terminates

Fix an embedding ℚ¯↪ℚ¯p\overline{\mathbb Q}\hookrightarrow\overline{\mathbb Q}_p and use a sufficient scan degree 2d2d from §139. Here dd fixes every special class under Frobenius. Good reduction makes the generic three-torsion unramified. The injective, equivariant specialization of classes via their three-torsion planes implies that inertia fixes each generic class and that the ddth power of Frobenius fixes it as well. Each generic quotient therefore descends locally as a genus-one quotient over the unramified extension Kd/ℚpK_d/\mathbb Q_p of degree dd. The evaluation determinant of §85 has degree two, so each marking is defined over an extension of KdK_d of degree at most two.

Write K2dK_{2d} for the unramified extension of degree 2d2d. All these marked fields embed into L=K2d(p)L=K_{2d}(\sqrt p). Indeed a unit of KdK_d is a square if and only if its residue is a square, by Hensel’s lemma. Adjoining the square root of a nonsquare residue unit gives K2dK_{2d}, and the remaining squareclass generator is pp. This argument includes marks that ramify or coalesce on reduction. It supplies one compact valuation ring R=𝒪LR=\mathcal O_L for the entire search. An unramified digit search alone can discard a genuine ramified marking.

The normalized chart data of a generic mark extend in at least one chart about its reduction. To see this, extend the elliptic quotient of the Jacobian and form the induced morphism of the curve into the corresponding genus-one torsor. Intrinsically one pushes out the relative Pic1\operatorname{Pic}^1 torsor along the quotient and composes the degree-one Abel map. The resulting map on the smooth special fibre has degree three by preservation of the polarization. The marked target point extends by properness, the fibre is finite flat of length three, and the canonical sections vanishing on it span a line in each fibre. Over the valuation ring this gives a primitive fibre line. Its residual point is a section. A degree-two target function at the mark is supplied by the relative space of sections of 2O2O: Riemann–Roch and base change give rank two and reduction onto the special space. The conic numerator can be scaled and translated integrally, since the coefficient of HNHN used in §125 is a unit on reduction. Together with chart I this covers every specialization of a normalized flag. The supplied moving tangent example exhibits the change of chart over the 5-adic integers.

For a marked state xnx_n modulo πn\pi^n with π=p\pi=\sqrt p, write its successors as xn+πnvx_n+\pi^n v, vv a vector over 𝔽p2d\mathbb F_{p^{2d}}. For the vector AA of chart equations solve (∂A/∂x)(x1)v=−A(xn)/πn(modπ). (\partial A/\partial x)(x_1)v=-A(x_n)/\pi^n\pmod\pi . Keep every solution of this affine linear system, including an entire kernel when the derivative drops rank. A special class survives if at least one of its marked branches survives. The number of surviving classes is an upper bound on the generic count at every precision. The rank of the derivative alone does not decide a singular lifting problem.

The tree is finitely branching. Survival to every precision gives an infinite compatible path by the finite-branching tree lemma. Completeness of RR gives a common zero of all equations on that path. The characteristic-zero generic fibre of either normalized chart has finite support by §125 and the change of frame above. A zero over LL thus has coordinates algebraic over ℚ\mathbb Q and yields an actual geometric class. Conversely every generic class has an integral marked branch by the extension argument. There are finitely many special classes, and distinct generic classes specialize distinctly. Consequently the decreasing sequence of upper bounds reaches the true geometric count after some finite, input-dependent precision.

To detect that point, enumerate exact positive certificates at the same time. An integral primitive element of a marked field has degree at most 1680 by §127. Enumerate monic irreducible integer polynomials through that degree, the two affine point coordinates, and the transverse line parameter in the represented field, with increasing common bounds on coefficient height and denominators. The tangent line is tested separately. At a transverse direction solve the quartic in §140 over the coefficient field, compute the forced linear coefficient, and check all shape residues. A true flag will occur because its coordinates, including the normalized conic, belong to its marked field. Check the resulting cubic net and count the entire Galois orbit once by the differential norm in §126. The increasing lower bound reaches the true count too. Equality certifies exhaustion. Finite congruence tests at several primes alone do not have this positive termination property. The implementation also attempts fast recovery directly from local digits before taking another step of the height enumeration.

An explicit family tests this distinction. A first-order obstruction even when every point has a genuine hit

Fix p=13p=13 and write F0=X4+Y4+Z4F_0=X^4+Y^4+Z^4. Let FF be an integral quartic congruent to F0F_0 modulo 13. At this ordinary prime the geometric Fermat reduction has exactly sixteen cubic quotient classes. Its 32 marked points are distinct and rational, and all occur in chart I with frame (0,1,2)(0,1,2). The finite scan supplies the 13 normalized chart coordinates for each marked state. A test of the original fifteen equations of §125 at precision 13213^2 can exclude all geometric characteristic-zero quotients, even after allowing arbitrary algebraic coefficient fields.

To justify the precision test, first note how a generic quotient produces an integral marked chart. After a finite extension of the complete local field, choose a source point, the elliptic subvariety and its torsion data. The source and Jacobian have good reduction. The elliptic factor has good reduction by the prime-to-pp Tate-module criterion. Its inclusion in the Jacobian and its dual extend to abelian schemes. The composition on the elliptic curve is [3][3], so any fibre kernel of the inclusion lies in the finite étale three-torsion. Injectivity on that torsion extends across good reduction. The quotient composed with Abel–Jacobi therefore gives a morphism from the smooth integral source model to the smooth elliptic model, of degree three on both fibres by the preserved polarization. It is finite flat by properness, quasi-finiteness, and flatness for maps of smooth curves over a discrete valuation ring. The determinant of §85 now defines the relative degree-two divisor of marks. Its special zeros are distinct here, so that divisor is finite étale. Each marked fibre line is the kernel line in the evaluation map; at a simple zero that map has rank two. Subtracting the degree-three fibre from its line section gives the integral residual point.

The chosen affine coordinate, partial derivative defining the frame, and the chart-I line pivot are units at the marked point. To normalize the conic pencil over the valuation ring, use the target sections with pole at most two at its marked image. This module is free of rank two and commutes with reduction by Riemann–Roch and cohomology and base change. On the source, restriction identifies conics with the six sections of 2KC2K_C in each fibre. Multiplication by the canonical section of twice the residual point gives the integral conic presentation of the pencil. Choose its denominator to be the square of the marked line, normalize the tangent-numerator coefficient to one, and remove its designated square term by translation. The divisions are by units because this special state belongs to the normalized chart. Finally the leading coefficient gg is a unit; the five square coefficients are determined through the top three powers of tt by division by 2g2g. Thus an actual generic quotient yields an integral solution reducing to one of the 32 tabulated states. This argument uses the good marked map, rather than an assertion that solutions of arbitrary affine equations are integral.

143. Projective reconstruction and the executed decisions

Projective CRT without matching roots or coordinate supports

For a prime pp record a finite set SpS_p of projective residue vectors of the same dimension. These can represent individual points, projective differential lines or the coefficients of the Chow form of an unordered cycle. For an effective cycle of two projective points P,QP,Q this form is (APX+BPY+CPZ)(AQX+BQY+CQZ)(A P_X+B P_Y+C P_Z)(A Q_X+B Q_Y+C Q_Z), up to nonzero scalar. For an inert quadratic pair write its point form as a+bθa+b\theta with θ2=sθ+t\theta^2=s\theta+t. Its norm is a2+sab−tb2a^2+sab-tb^2. This computes the same projective datum as the split product. It permits inert and split primes in the same reconstruction without choosing an identification of roots across primes.

Let HH bound the maximum absolute coefficient of a primitive integral representative and MM be the product of the selected distinct primes. For each choice vp∈Spv_p\in S_p, intersect the congruence lattices Λ={v∈ℤn:vmodp∈⟨vp⟩for every selected p}. \Lambda=\{v\in\mathbb Z^n:v\bmod p\in\langle v_p\rangle\ \text{for every selected }p\}. Any two compatible primitive vectors v,wv,w have all two-by-two minors divisible by MM. If M>2H2M>2H^2, the absolute values of the minors are smaller than MM, so [v]=[w][v]=[w]. A primitive vector is nonzero on reduction at every prime. This is projective height of the entire coefficient vector; bounding the height of one affine coordinate is a different condition.

The code starts with a column basis BB of the current lattice. Modulo a new prime it is invertible, since its index only involves the earlier primes. Normalize B−1vpB^{-1}v_p at one nonzero entry. Replace the corresponding column of pIpI by that normalized vector and multiply BB by the resulting matrix. The new index factor is pn−1p^{n-1}. Exact lattice reduction changes the basis and preserves the lattice. Bounded enumeration uses rational Gram–Schmidt projections and integer square-root endpoints for the ball ∥v∥22≤nH2\|v\|_2^2\le nH^2. Each retained answer is checked for primitivity, height and all original congruences. Searching a subset of primes already above the minor bound and filtering at the remaining primes saves work. The bound is a reconstruction theorem conditional on the supplied panels and height. The local lifting procedure has a separate, unbounded stopping rule for exhaustion.

At height seven the archived panels recover the two rational points on each positive rational example. At height two the four split panels for C2C_2 recover A2+B2+C2−AB−AC−BC. A^2+B^2+C^2-AB-AC-BC. A direct boxed enumeration also matches the lattice routine below the uniqueness threshold. Exact substitution in the quartic and the subsequent map identities supply the characteristic-zero verification.

Equation-only execution on the §136 inputs

The driver starts with the primitive integral quartic. The fast positive step reconstructs the point and line coefficients from local digits, solves the forced conics in characteristic zero and checks their map degree with the cubic net. The independent height enumeration makes the geometric stopping rule unconditional. In the shorter rational-class mode the upper bound counts Frobenius-fixed classes visible in a quadratic scan. 144. The Fermat quartic in every characteristic greater than three

When supersingular reduction preserves the sixteen cubic classes. For every p>16p>16, reduction of the Fermat quartic has exactly the same sixteen geometric degree-three quotient classes as in characteristic zero, including at the supersingular primes p≡3(mod4)p\equiv3\pmod4. The 16 characteristic-zero classes give two distinct transverse marks apiece at both primes. At 7 all 48 additional classes occur with exactly one tangent marked point over 𝔽49\mathbb F_{49}, and every one of the 64 classes occurs in that field’s scan. Each additional class has a double mark: its complete rational degree-two mark divisor contains one rational point, so a residual degree-one point would also have to be rational and would appear in the exhaustive scan. These are genuine special classes that do not lift to the integral Fermat curve in characteristic zero. All 48 are non-Galois triple covers. Indeed an automorphism of the canonical quartic preserves its Hessian divisor, given by X2Y2Z2X^2Y^2Z^2 for p>3p>3, so it permutes the three axes. The full automorphism group is the monomial group of order 96 with diagonal subgroup of order 16. It has exactly sixteen subgroups of order three: each order-three permutation has sixteen diagonal lifts, all of order three projectively, and each subgroup has two generators. The sixteen cyclic degree-three quotients already account for these subgroups.

One ramified obstruction eliminates the entire jump. The 48 tangent marks form one orbit under the coordinate permutations and diagonal fourth roots, as a direct enumeration on their projective coordinates verifies. These automorphisms lift to the integral Fermat model over the unramified quadratic extension of ℚ7\mathbb Q_7. Use 𝔽49=𝔽7[θ]/(θ2+1)\mathbb F_{49}=\mathbb F_7[\theta]/(\theta^2+1) and take the orbit representative (3+3θ:1:1)(3+3\theta:1:1). Its residual point is a double mark. An arbitrary geometric characteristic-zero lift would give its class over an unramified field by the étale three-torsion injection, and a mark over at most a quadratic extension of that field. Over the maximal unramified extension every tamely ramified quadratic extension is generated by ϖ=7\varpi=\sqrt{7}. It suffices to test integral marked lifts over this ring with algebraically closed residue field.

In the open chart permitting a deformation of the tangent line, let GG be the full integral incidence system and x0x_0 the unramified digit representative of the modular solution. Its thirteen-variable Jacobian JJ has rank twelve and kernel spanned by vv. The first ramified digit is necessarily ava v. In the second ramified digit test modulo ϖ3\varpi^3, the equation on x=x0+ϖav+ϖ2wx=x_0+\varpi a v+\varpi^2 w is Jw+a2h+b=0,b=G(x0)/7mod7. Jw+a^2 h+b=0,\qquad b=G(x_0)/7\bmod7 . The lack of a linear aa term here follows because the base coefficients and digit representatives are unramified, and JvJv at those representatives is already divisible by seven. The column hh is the quadratic Hasse coefficient, obtained by subtracting bb from the second residual digit at x0+ϖvx_0+\varpi v. Over 𝔽49\mathbb F_{49} the respective ranks of J,[J∣h],[J∣h∣b]J,[J\mid h],[J\mid h\mid b] are 12, 13, 14. They persist over the algebraic closure, so even allowing an arbitrary scalar in place of a2a^2 cannot give a solution. The entire orbit of 48 double-marked special classes is therefore excluded by the third ramified digit alone. The surviving sixteen classes lift by their explicit cyclic maps. The geometric special count of 64 and the certified characteristic-zero count of sixteen are thus connected by a single-prime, finite-precision calculation.

The integral polarization and the full degree spectrum

Let JJ be the principally polarized Jacobian. The pullback of E0E_0 embeds with polarization degree three; a nontrivial intermediate isogeny for a prime-degree map would leave degree one. Let PP be its connected orthogonal complement. The map J→E0∨J\to E_0^\vee dual to the inclusion has connected kernel PP. Its restriction to E0E_0 is multiplication by three up to principal identifications. Thus E0∩P=E0[3]E_0\cap P=E_0[3] and the addition isogeny E0×P→JE_0\times P\to J has degree nine. Taking Euler characteristics of its pullback polarization gives 9=3χ(Θ|P)9=3\chi(\Theta|_P), so χ(Θ|P)=3\chi(\Theta|_P)=3.

Let j:E′↪Jj:E'\hookrightarrow J be the pullback for a transposition. It has polarization degree two. The action of ρ\rho on the tangent line of E0E_0 is trivial, and a transposition acts on this line by −1-1. Indeed ρ\rho fixes the HH-line of canonical differentials, and the determinant −1-1 in the residue transformation changes the sign of HH under a transposition. The dual tangent representation has the same invariant lines and the same sign. The line of jj is transposition-invariant with sign +1+1, hence has zero component in the ρ\rho-fixed line. On the remaining two-dimensional summand 1+ρ+ρ2=01+\rho+\rho^2=0. It follows, by taking differentials in characteristic zero, that j+ρj+ρ2j=0j+\rho j+\rho^2j=0, with all three images in PP. The images of j,ρjj,\rho j are distinct: the transposition interchanges the two distinct nontrivial ρ\rho-eigenlines, so its fixed line is neither of them. Therefore ψ=(j,ρj):(E′)2→P\psi=(j,\rho j):(E')^2\to P is an isogeny by addition.

On (E′)2(E')^2 the symmetric matrix of the pulled-back polarization in the principal units of E′E' is integral, since End(E′)=ℤ\operatorname{End}(E')=\mathbb Z. Its diagonal is (2,2)(2,2) and its off-diagonal entry is −1-1, since j+ρj=−ρ2jj+\rho j=-\rho^2j also has degree two. Rational maps in every degree

For each of the three positive §136 examples the complete map spectrum over ℚ\mathbb Q is {3n2:n≥1}, \{3n^2:n\ge1\}, with one class in each indicated degree up to rational target isomorphism and translation. In the rationally marked examples there is only one geometric optimal quotient. On C2C_2 all other optimal quotients have a nontrivial cubic class field, and rationality of any map implies rationality of its optimal quotient by taking the connected kernel of the induced Jacobian homomorphism. Each source has a rational point, so all the required target origins exist.

It remains to determine the rational isogenies out of the unique rational optimal target EE. Mazur’s prime-isogeny theorem restricts possible degrees of a rational prime isogeny to 2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19,37,43,67,1632,3,5,7,11,13,17,19,37,43,67,163. The traces are computed directly by summing the quadratic character of each cubic or quartic model and counting points at infinity. B. Mazur, Rational isogenies of prime degree, Theorem 1 (1978).

The three transpositions in this family are Galois-conjugate: the rational three-cycle permutes them transitively, so Galois acts through the centralizer of that cycle, a cyclic group of order three. 147. A rational contact octic for twists with nonsplit axes

A rational octic for every plane twist of Fermat

The split-axis result of §128 extends to a point-free detector for every rational plane form of the geometric Fermat quartic, even when its three diagonal axes are permuted by Galois. Polarize FF in four arguments and let HFH_F be its matrix of second derivatives. Solve the rational linear equations HFM=M𝗍HFH_F M=M^{\mathsf t}H_F coefficient by coefficient. In diagonal coordinates all their solutions are diagonal matrices. Conversely if a solution has three distinct eigenvalues, the symmetry of polarization allows MM to move between any two arguments. A mixed coefficient supported on eigenvectors of distinct eigenvalues vanishes. Thus the three eigendirections diagonalize FF. On a smooth source each fourth-power coefficient is nonzero. For a geometric Fermat form the solution algebra has dimension three. For a rational basis M0,M1,M2M_0,M_1,M_2 a matrix M0+nM1+n2M2M_0+nM_1+n^2M_2 has squarefree characteristic polynomial for some 0≤n≤120\le n\le12: the discriminant has degree at most twelve and is nonzero since the three diagonal-entry functionals are distinct. This is an equation-only recognition test over ℚ\mathbb Q.

Write F=A0+A1+A2F=A_0+A_1+A_2 over the splitting field with Ai=aiLi4A_i=a_i L_i^4. Let hh be the squarefree part of detHF\det H_F, a rational scalar multiple of L0L1L2L_0 L_1 L_2. Set δ=det(Hh)/h\delta=\det(H_h)/h; it is a nonzero rational constant. Compute the octic ℳF=F24+(∇F)𝗍adj(Hh)∇F32δ. \mathcal M_F=\frac{F^2}{4}+\frac{(\nabla F)^{\mathsf t}\operatorname{adj}(H_h)\nabla F}{32\delta}. Then ℳF=∑i<jAiAj\mathcal M_F=\sum_{i<j}A_iA_j. In the frame h=XYZh=XYZ, δ=2\delta=2 and the contraction is 16(−∑Ai2+2∑i<jAiAj)16(-\sum A_i^2+2\sum_{i<j}A_iA_j). The two determinant weights and the scalar ambiguity of hh cancel in the ratio. This proves the identity in rational coordinates without extracting any axis or taking fourth roots.

The complete intersection F=ℳF=0F=\mathcal M_F=0 consists of precisely the 32 reduced marked residual points. Indeed, in the split frame their fourth-power values are proportional, in some order, to (1,ω,ω2)(1,\omega,\omega^2). On the torus the fourth-power map is étale and there are two distinct ordered ratios after normalizing the last one. The resulting 2⋅422\cdot4^2 points exhaust the Bézout degree. The Gauss map P↦[∇F(P)]P\mapsto[\nabla F(P)] gives the sixteen quotient differential lines, two marks per line. In scaled Fermat coordinates each such line is U+V+W=0U+V+W=0, whose restriction is 2(U2+UV+V2)22(U^2+UV+V^2)^2. Its two contacts are the eigenpoints of cyclic permutation. The other two invariant eigenlines of the permutation supply the marked collinear fibres; the contact point on each is its residual point. Conversely §128 accounts for every geometric cubic quotient. To check that these are exactly the ordinary bitangents, normalize a line with three nonzero entries and substitute W=−U−VW=-U-V. The nonzero fourth-power coefficients force d2=2d^2=2, which fixes the two axis scalings. A line with a missing entry instead must cut out a quadruple point to be a bitangent. There are twelve such hyperflex lines.

148. What is now certified

The missing steps in §137 have executable forms. Both pencil charts work over prime-power fields, a finite extension degree captures every geometric special class, and digit lifting with exact characteristic-zero recovery supplies a stopping test. The choice of characteristic and the size of its required extension still dominate cost. The implemented finite-field arithmetic builds full addition and multiplication tables. This makes the listed small-field results easy to replay, while the theoretical extreme of a degree-80 residue field is beyond that implementation’s practical reach. A bounded run prints both bounds if they have yet to meet. A Frobenius-fixed special class and a rational elliptic origin are separate conditions, and general rational-point determination on the resulting genus-one targets remains open.

The archive contains the quartic inputs, both independent first-order constructions, the conormal matrices, field and class counts, explicit map identities and single-prime decision outputs. The full paper and its replay instructions are in scan_completeness_xxx/. The earlier atlas timing is retained as a historical benchmark. None of the measured runtimes or bounds implies a uniform practical runtime for arbitrary quartics.
